title: getInventory calls GET /articles/inventory — endpoint does not exist in Ongoing REST API; use GET /articles inventoryInfo
description: From audit MedusaOngoingWarehousePlugin-s1k (R2, dim 2; report: docs/audits/2026-07-15-s1k-wms-integration-audit.md). Ongoing openapi.json?version=57 has no /api/v1/articles/inventory path (verified by machine inspection). Inventory is exposed via GET /api/v1/articles (inventoryInfo per GetArticleModel), /articles/inventoryPerWarehouse, or /articles/historicalInventory. Every stock-sync tick will 404 (classified terminal) against a real tenant. Also: the CSV filter param is articleNumbers (plural), not articleNumber. Fix src/lib/ongoing/client.ts getInventory + align OngoingInventoryRowResponseSchema (src/lib/ongoing/schemas.ts) to the real GetArticleModel/inventoryInfo shape (SellableNumberOfItems etc. per https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/inventory).

Verified vs OpenAPI v57 GetArticleModel/GetArticleInventoryInfo. Tests: client.operations.test.ts (endpoint + articleNumbers CSV), client.rest-edge-validation.test.ts, schemas.test.ts.

title: client.ts paginates with nonexistent page/pageSize params — infinite-loop risk; switch to Ongoing cursor pagination
description: From audit MedusaOngoingWarehousePlugin-s1k (R1, dim 5; report: docs/audits/2026-07-15-s1k-wms-integration-audit.md). Machine-inspection of Ongoing REST openapi.json?version=57 shows 'page'/'pageSize' appear 0 times in the spec. Real pagination is ID-cursor: GET /orders uses orderIdFrom+maxOrdersToGet, GET /articles uses articleSystemIdFrom+maxArticlesToGet; last page detected via empty response (https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/paginating-responses). Today every 'page' in OngoingClient.paginate() issues the identical request, so any result set >= ONGOING_PAGE_SIZE (50) loops forever inside the every-minute status-poll/stock-sync jobs and duplicates rows. Fix src/lib/ongoing/client.ts paginate/getOrdersByStatus/getInventory to cursor pagination terminating on empty batch.
notes: Fixed in client.ts: replaced fictional page/pageSize with cursor pagination — paginateByCursor() drives GET /orders by orderIdFrom+maxOrdersToGet and GET /articles by articleSystemIdFrom+maxArticlesToGet, terminating on empty/short batch. Added a non-advance guard (maxId seeded from batch, stop if cursor can't move past cursorFrom) so a server ignoring the cursor can't loop. Verified vs OpenAPI v57 (params confirmed present; page/pageSize confirmed absent). Regression tests: client.orders-by-status.test.ts (cursor params, no page/pageSize, advance-past-max, non-advance guard) + client.operations.test.ts (articles cursor).
close_reason: Fixed against OpenAPI v57; regression tests added; lint+build clean, jest 468 passed/75 suites.

title: Goods owner id field does not appear in the admin Create integration modal despite being present in the shipped bundle
description:
REPORTED by Thomas 2026-08-07, twice. The Goods owner id field added in 9y2.9 is not visible in Settings -> Ongoing Warehouse -> Create integration in the running b2b app.

THIS IS NOT A MISSING-CODE PROBLEM. Verified present at every layer:
- source: src/admin/routes/settings/ongoing/integration-form-fields.tsx has the Label + Input with id 'ongoing-goods-owner-id' (plugin main, merged as eefbe76).
- plugin build: .medusa/server/src/admin/index.js contains 10 references incl. the rendered Label/Input.
- app .yalc copy: apps/backend/.yalc/@comfyballs/.../.medusa/server/src/admin/index.js — present.
- app node_modules copy: apps/backend/node_modules/@comfyballs/.../.medusa/server/src/admin/index.js — present.
So the failure lies in admin BUNDLING/CACHING between node_modules and the browser.

PRIME SUSPECT — Vite optimizeDeps cache keyed on an unchanged version. The plugin has been rebuilt and re-linked many times while its version stayed pinned at 0.0.1. Medusa's admin is bundled by Vite, which pre-bundles dependencies and caches them (apps/backend/node_modules/.vite/ exists) keyed on package identity/version and lockfile, NOT on file: dependency content. That fits the symptom exactly: SERVER-side plugin code updates fine (the API routes /admin/ongoing/credential-keys and /ongoing/webhooks/main both answer 401, i.e. registered), while the Vite-bundled ADMIN extensions stay stale. Server code is loaded by Node at boot; admin code goes through the cached Vite pipeline.

CONTRIBUTING FACTOR — two dev servers running at once (:9000 and :9001), same working tree, same apps/backend/node_modules/.vite cache directory. Both currently serve the plugin API routes. They can populate/reuse each other's cache, and it is not obvious which one the browser points at. Earlier this session the same confusion produced a 'Failed to load credential keys' report that turned out to be a stale :9000 with no plugin at all.

TRY IN THIS ORDER:
1. Stop BOTH dev servers so only one runs; confirm the port in the browser address bar.
2. Delete the Vite cache directory apps/backend/node_modules/.vite (and apps/backend/.medusa/cache), restart, hard-reload the browser with cache disabled.
3. If that fixes it, the durable fix is to stop shipping identical versions: bump the plugin version on every local publish, or use 'yalc push --changed' / a prerelease suffix so Vite sees a new identity. Document the outcome in docs/wiki/Dev-Local-App-Testing.md — every future admin-UI change hits this same trap.
4. If it does NOT fix it, next suspects: Medusa admin extension discovery (does it enumerate plugin admin routes only at dev-server start?), and whether 'medusa develop' needs an explicit admin rebuild after a linked package changes.

DO NOT re-verify by grepping node_modules — already confirmed clean. Verify by loading the modal in a browser on a known port with caches cleared.
acceptance_criteria:
- The Goods owner id field renders in Create integration, between Credential key and Stock location, and is disabled when editing an existing integration.
- Entering a goods owner + credential key enables Test connection, and it succeeds against the Ongoing sandbox (goods owner 362).
- Creating an integration persists goods_owner_id on the row.
- Root cause identified and the fix written into docs/wiki/Dev-Local-App-Testing.md so the next admin-UI change does not lose the same hour.
notes:
Environment at filing: plugin repo on main @ eefbe76 (goods-owner work merged, L1 742/742, L2 51/51). b2b repo on develop @ b2fbc0a with the flat single-credential config; apps/backend/.env has ONGOING_BASE_URL/_USER/_PASSWORD/_WEBHOOK_SECRET and no goods owner (correct — it is admin data now). ongoing_integration has the goods_owner_id column (NOT NULL) with zero rows. Both :9000 and :9001 answered /health 200 at filing time.

Gotcha already learned this session, worth not relearning: 'medusa plugin:publish' only refreshes the GLOBAL yalc store — the consuming app additionally needs 'yalc update' in apps/backend to pull it. That step fixed an earlier stale-build failure and may be part of whatever fix lands here.
close_reason: Not a code or bundling defect. Root cause was the duplicate dev server: a stale Medusa instance on :9000 (Homebrew Node 26) was serving an old admin bundle alongside the current one on :9001 (nvm Node 24.18.0). Stopping both and restarting a single server made the Goods owner id field appear immediately — no cache clear or version bump needed. The Vite optimizeDeps theory in the description was NOT the cause; leaving it recorded because it remains a plausible trap for a genuine stale-bundle case later. Second false bug report this session from the same duplicate-server confusion (the first was 'Failed to load credential keys').

title: Move goodsOwnerId from plugin options to the integration row; one shared credential set in env
description:
DECIDED by Thomas 2026-08-06. One Ongoing API account (base URL + user + password) serves the tenant; each warehouse is a separate GOODS OWNER under that account. So the goods-owner id is per-integration operator data, not a credential, and belongs in the admin UI on the OngoingIntegration row — not in medusa-config.

This supersedes 9y2.8 (keyed per-warehouse env vars): the app env collapses back to ONE flat credential set, and multiple warehouses become multiple integration ROWS sharing it, each with its own goods_owner_id and its own dedicated stock location.

BLAST RADIUS — 46 files reference goodsOwnerId/goods_owner_id, but almost all merely thread it through as a step/mapper parameter and need no change. Only two sites SOURCE it:
  - src/workflows/steps/resolve-integration-context.ts:35  goods_owner_id: creds.goodsOwnerId
  - src/workflows/steps/upsert-ongoing-order-edit.ts:52    service.getCredentials(key).goodsOwnerId
Both switch to reading integration.goods_owner_id.

WORK:
1. Model + migration: goods_owner_id on OngoingIntegration. Safe as a required column — the package is unpublished and the only table in existence (b2b dev) has zero rows.
2. Types/options: drop goodsOwnerId from OngoingCredentials; update validateOngoingOptions and its INVALID_DATA messages.
3. Client: OngoingClient reads this.creds.goodsOwnerId in three query strings (client.ts:165,187,212). Take the goods-owner id explicitly instead.
4. Service: getClient must key its client/Throttle cache by (credential_key, goods_owner_id) rather than credential_key alone.
5. The two source sites above.
6. Admin UI: goods-owner field on the create/edit integration form.
7. API validators + integration CRUD workflows: accept and persist goods_owner_id.
8. Docs: plugin User-Configuration-Reference / User-Setup-Guide / Dev-Architecture; b2b docs/environment-variables.md + .env.template back to flat vars.
9. Tests: L1 + L2.

DESIGN NOTE worth a second opinion before merge: splitting the client cache by goods owner also splits the Throttle, which today serializes all calls per credential key. Dev-Architecture states the intent is to serialize per GOODS OWNER (matching Ongoing's parallel-requests guidance), so per-(key, goodsOwner) is arguably more correct — but if Ongoing rate-limits per API USER instead, this raises concurrency against one account. Confirm against Ongoing's docs.
acceptance_criteria:
- medusa-config carries only baseUrl/username/password/webhookSecret; no goodsOwnerId anywhere in plugin options.
- An integration is created in the admin with a goods-owner id, and that id is what reaches Ongoing (verified against the sandbox, goods owner 362).
- Two integration rows with DIFFERENT goods owners under ONE credential set each talk to their own goods owner.
- Boot validation no longer requires or mentions goodsOwnerId.
- L1 + L2 green; lint + build clean.
- Plugin and b2b docs updated in the same change.
notes:
IN PROGRESS 2026-08-06. WIP commit 16dce65 on branch feat/9y2.9-goods-owner-per-integration (plugin repo). DO NOT MERGE — 5 test suites / 9 tests still failing.

STATE: all PRODUCTION code type-clean (0 tsc errors outside tests). L1 732/741 passing.

NOTE: the column is 'not null' with no default, so it would fail on a table with existing rows — fine here (package unpublished, the only table in existence has zero rows) but it must be revisited before any real deployment carries data.
- OngoingCredentials no longer has goodsOwnerId; validateOngoingOptions updated.
- OngoingClient takes goodsOwnerId as a REQUIRED opt. Making it required rather than optional is what surfaced all 11 call sites at compile time instead of letting one silently emit goodsOwnerId=undefined.

- Both SOURCE sites repointed to integration.goods_owner_id; four step input types (cancel-ongoing-order, fetch-ongoing-inventory, fetch-ongoing-order-lines, push-return-order) gained the field, plus the workflows that build them.

- test-connection route + validator take goods_owner_id; admin form has the field, disabled on edit (immutable like credential_key / stock_location_id).

REMAINING:

2. Docs: plugin User-Configuration-Reference / User-Setup-Guide / Dev-Architecture.
3. b2b app: collapse env back to ONE flat credential set (ONGOING_BASE_URL / _USER / _PASSWORD / _WEBHOOK_SECRET, no goods owner). Commit 5e1ecfc on feat/ongoing-plugin-env-gated-registration is already close — it has the flat vars; only ONGOING_GOODS_OWNER_ID needs removing. The keyed-env variant from superseded 9y2.8 was never committed and is gone from the working tree, which is fine.

title: Make the b2b Ongoing env convention per-warehouse (goods owner, credentials, webhook secret per integration)
description:
The plugin takes an integrations ARRAY — each entry is one Ongoing goods owner with its own key, baseUrl, username, password, goodsOwnerId and webhookSecret, bound one-to-one to a Medusa stock location. The b2b app config from 9y2.2 flattened that to a single set of env vars (ONGOING_BASE_URL / ONGOING_GOODS_OWNER_ID / ...) plus a hardcoded ONGOING_CREDENTIAL_KEY = 'main', so the app can only ever address one warehouse. Adding a second goods owner would require a config edit rather than an env change.

Replace it with a keyed convention: ONGOING_WAREHOUSE_KEYS lists the credential keys, and each key K contributes ONGOING_<K>_BASE_URL / _USER / _PASSWORD / _GOODS_OWNER_ID / _WEBHOOK_SECRET. The credential key stops being a hardcoded constant and becomes data, which is right — it is per-warehouse, permanent once orders exist (embedded in /ongoing/webhooks/<key> and stored on every sync row), and each goods owner needs its own dedicated stock location.

Named per-key vars rather than one JSON blob: Medusa Cloud sets env per environment through a UI, where discrete named variables are far easier to manage than JSON, and it matches the app's existing UNOPIM_* / MEILISEARCH_* / GOOGLE_* style. Keep the all-or-nothing gate and the partial-configuration warning, now reporting exactly which key is missing which var.
acceptance_criteria:
- ONGOING_WAREHOUSE_KEYS with one key registers one integration; with two keys registers two, each with its own goodsOwnerId.
- A key missing any of its five vars warns naming the exact variables and registers nothing.
- No ONGOING_* set at all: no warning, app boots unchanged.
- .env.template and docs/environment-variables.md describe the keyed convention.
- Verified against the running app: the admin credential-keys dropdown lists every configured key.

title: Link the plugin into apps/backend for local development and boot the app clean
description:
The actual local install, on a branch in the b2b repo, with the dependency change kept OUT of any commit that reaches Medusa Cloud.

- Build the plugin (yarn build → .medusa/server) or run yarn dev for a yalc watch build. Note the plugin repo is yarn 4 while the app is pnpm — pnpm can consume a yalc-published package, but yalc rewrites apps/backend/package.json and creates .yalc/; add both to the b2b .gitignore and never commit the dependency line.
- Alternative worth trying first, and probably simpler under pnpm's hoisted node-linker: 'pnpm add <tarball>' from 'yarn pack', or a pnpm overrides entry pointing at the local build. Pick whichever gives a single @medusajs/framework in the tree.
- Set the ONGOING_* env vars in apps/backend/.env from this repo's .env.integration sandbox credentials.
- Boot 'pnpm dev' and confirm: no duplicate framework, the validate-options loader logs '[ongoing] validated N warehouse integration(s)', the ongoing module resolves, and the plugin's jobs (status-poll, stock-sync every 15m, retry-failed-syncs every 5m) and subscribers register without error.
- Confirm the plugin's src/links defineLink associations are discovered from an installed package (they are declared inside the plugin, not the app) — this is the first time that path is exercised outside the in-repo L2 fixture.
acceptance_criteria:
- apps/backend boots with the plugin loaded and logs the validate-options success line.
- 'pnpm why @medusajs/framework' shows one version.
- Plugin jobs and subscribers appear in the boot log with no errors.
- git status in the b2b repo shows no committed dependency or .yalc artifacts.
close_reason: Plugin linked into apps/backend via yalc and booted clean in the real app: '[ongoing] validated 1 warehouse integration(s)', server ready on :9001, exactly one @medusajs/framework (2.18.0) in the tree, and fulfillment_provider now holds manual_manual AND ongoing_ongoing both enabled. Route probes confirm registration: /ongoing/webhooks/main and /admin/ongoing/integrations both 401 while a bogus path 404s.

title: Deploy safety: env-gated Ongoing registration in the b2b medusa-config, with a CI proof the app deploys without the plugin
description:
This is the 'we must still be able to deploy the b2b app without this plugin' guarantee. Do it FIRST — it has no dependency on the plugin being installable, and it is what makes every later step safe. Lands in the medusa-b2b-prototype repo, not here.

WHY IT WORKS BEFORE THE PACKAGE EXISTS: Medusa registers plugins and fulfillment providers by resolve-STRING, not by import. A branch of the config that is never evaluated never resolves the package, so the gated config is completely inert on an environment with no ONGOING_* env vars — safe to merge to the b2b main long before the plugin is publishable.

WORK (apps/backend/medusa-config.ts), copying the UnoPIM block at lines ~71-118 verbatim in shape:
- const ONGOING_ENV_VARS = [ONGOING_BASE_URL, ONGOING_USER, ONGOING_PASSWORD, ONGOING_GOODS_OWNER_ID, ONGOING_WEBHOOK_SECRET] (final names per the plugin's User-Configuration-Reference); ongoingConfigured = every var present; partial-configuration console.warn exactly like UnoPIM's, because the failure mode otherwise is a silent 'Could not resolve ongoing' downstream.
- const ongoingPlugin = !isTestEnv && ongoingConfigured ? [{ resolve: <pkg name>, options: { integrations: [...], rateLimitConcurrency: 1 } }] : []  → spread into a top-level plugins: [...ongoingPlugin] key (the config has no plugins key today).
- Fulfillment provider — THE DANGEROUS PART. The app declares no [Modules.FULFILLMENT] today, and @medusajs/fulfillment/dist/loaders/providers.js syncDatabaseProviders() sets is_enabled=false on every fulfillment_provider row absent from the configured options.providers. The DB currently holds exactly one row, manual_manual (enabled), and initial-data-seed.ts wires every service zone and shipping option to it. So the new [Modules.FULFILLMENT] entry MUST list @medusajs/medusa/fulfillment-manual (id 'manual') unconditionally, with the ongoing provider spread in only when configured. Snapshot the provider rows before and after boot and prove manual_manual stayed enabled.
- Also decide and document the reverse direction: once ongoing_* provider rows exist, un-setting the env vars disables them and breaks any shipping option bound to them. Toggling the integration off is NOT free — say so in a comment next to the gate.
- Add the ONGOING_* vars to apps/backend/.env.template and docs/environment-variables.md, commented as optional.

CI: extend .github/workflows/ci.yml so the existing build job (or a new one) proves a no-ONGOING_* build+boot is clean — the same class of guard the repo already added for the UnoPIM admin route in #358.
acceptance_criteria:
- With no ONGOING_* env vars: apps/backend builds and boots with zero new warnings or errors, and 'select id, is_enabled from fulfillment_provider' is unchanged from before the commit (manual_manual still enabled).
- With a partial ONGOING_* set: a single clear console.warn, module NOT registered, app still boots.
- With the full set (and the package installed): the plugin and the ongoing fulfillment provider both register, AND manual_manual is still enabled.
- A CI job fails if the app stops building/booting without the plugin.
- ONGOING_* documented as optional in .env.template and docs/environment-variables.md.
- No local-path dependency (yalc/file:/link:) in the committed apps/backend/package.json; .yalc/ and yalc.lock added to that repo's .gitignore.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-03. Committed as b73dc7e on branch feat/ongoing-plugin-env-gated-registration in /Volumes/Projects/medusa-b2b-prototype (not pushed, not merged).

Files: apps/backend/medusa-config.ts, apps/backend/.env.template, docs/environment-variables.md, .gitignore.

Env var names chosen (app-side convention, matching UNOPIM_*): ONGOING_BASE_URL, ONGOING_USER, ONGOING_PASSWORD, ONGOING_GOODS_OWNER_ID, ONGOING_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Credential key hardcoded to 'main' — it is embedded in the webhook path /ongoing/webhooks/main and stored on every sync row, so it is permanent once orders exist.

VERIFIED (Node 24.18.0, no ONGOING_* set):
- fulfillment_provider rows after a boot on the new config: manual_manual, is_enabled=t — unchanged. This was the main risk: declaring [Modules.FULFILLMENT] to add the ongoing provider makes syncDatabaseProviders disable every unlisted provider, and this app seeds all shipping options against manual_manual. 'manual' is listed unconditionally.
- The boot used for that check died on EADDRINUSE (a dev server already held :9000), but the fulfillment provider loader runs during module loading, well before HTTP listen — the log shows Redis connected and links/workflows/subscribers/jobs all loaded, so the loader definitely ran.
- Partial-config path: with only 2 of 5 vars set, warns '[medusa-config] Ongoing Warehouse is only partially configured (missing ONGOING_PASSWORD / ONGOING_GOODS_OWNER_ID / ONGOING_WEBHOOK_SECRET)' and continues booting.
- integration-tests/http/booking/partial-delivery-drop.spec.ts: 2/2 pass, and the log shows a real order.fulfillment_created + shipment.created through the manual provider under the new explicit module declaration.
- typecheck clean; lint 0 errors (58 pre-existing warnings, none in touched files); pnpm build clean (backend + admin).

NO NEW CI JOB NEEDED — the acceptance criterion is already met by existing jobs, which is a better outcome than adding machinery: the 'build' job runs pnpm build with no ONGOING_* set, and the 4-way-sharded 'integration-http' job boots the full app across ~70 suites, 17 of which reference manual_manual. A regression in either the gate or the provider list turns those red.

NOT DONE (deliberately, belongs to 9y2.3): the actual plugin install. package.json is untouched, so nothing depends on the plugin yet.

Deploy safety verified: manual_manual still enabled after boot, partial-config warns and boots, a real fulfillment created through the manual provider in the http suite, typecheck/lint/build clean with no ONGOING_* set. Existing build + integration-http CI jobs already serve as the no-plugin deploy proof.

title: Make the plugin installable by a Medusa 2.18.0 / pnpm / Node 24 app (peer ranges + distribution)
description:
Blocks every other child. Two independent problems.

A) VERSION RANGE. package.json pins every @medusajs/* peerDependency to an EXACT 2.16.0; the target app is on 2.18.0. With the app's .npmrc (strict-peer-dependencies=false, auto-install-peers=true, node-linker=hoisted) pnpm resolves a second @medusajs/framework@2.16.0 rather than failing — two framework copies in one process break Awilix registration identity, MedusaService base classes and defineLink, with confusing symptoms.
  - Widen peerDependencies to a range that admits 2.18.0 (e.g. '>=2.16.0 <3.0.0'), keeping devDependencies as the pinned dev target.
  - Actually verify against 2.18.0, do not assume: install 2.18.0 into a scratch resolution, run yarn build, yarn lint, yarn test (L1) and the L2 full-app harness. Diff the 2.16→2.18 changelog for anything this plugin touches: fulfillment provider abstract class, MedusaService, defineLink, query.graph, workflow SDK, admin UI (@medusajs/ui 4.1.16 vs the app's 4.2.0).
  - Decide whether to also bump this repo's own devDependency pin to 2.18.0 to match the production consumer. Recommendation: yes, once the suite is green, so the plugin is developed against what it ships onto.

B) DISTRIBUTION. The package cannot currently be installed by the app at all:
  - name 'MedusaOngoingWarehousePlugin' contains uppercase, which npm rejects for new packages, and it is unpublished (registry 404).
  - a git dependency does not work either: files is ['.medusa/server'], .medusa is gitignored, and the build hook is prepublishOnly — npm/pnpm run 'prepare' on git installs, not prepublishOnly, so a git install delivers an empty package.
  Pick one and implement it: (i) rename to a lowercase scoped name (e.g. @comfyballs/medusa-plugin-ongoing-warehouse) and publish to GitHub Packages from the private repo — recommended, it is the only option that also works unchanged on Medusa Cloud; or (ii) keep the name for now and add a 'prepare' script so a git+ssh dependency builds on install — cheaper, but Medusa Cloud needs deploy-key access to the private repo. A rename touches every resolve-string in docs and in the b2b config, so decide BEFORE child 9y2.3 writes those strings.

C) NODE. App engines node>=24 with engine-strict=true; this plugin declares >=20 and is known to crash lint/build on Node 26. Confirm the plugin builds under Node 24 and widen engines accordingly.
design:
DECIDED 2026-07-31 (Thomas, explicit approval):

1. RENAME the package. New name: @comfyballs/medusa-plugin-ongoing-warehouse. The scope is forced — GitHub Packages requires the npm scope to match the repo owner (github.com/Comfyballs), and npm scopes must be lowercase. Distribution is option (i) from the description: publish to GitHub Packages from the private repo. This is the only distribution that works unchanged on Medusa Cloud, which builds from git and cannot resolve yalc/file:/link: deps.
   Consequence: every 'resolve:' string changes — plugin entry, the fulfillment provider path (@comfyballs/medusa-plugin-ongoing-warehouse/providers/ongoing-fulfillment), and every docs/wiki example. Must land BEFORE 9y2.3 writes those strings into the b2b medusa-config.

2. BUMP the dev pin to Medusa 2.18.0, matching the production consumer, once the suite is green against it. Rationale: develop against what we ship onto. devDependencies move 2.16.0 -> 2.18.0 (and @medusajs/ui 4.1.16 -> 4.2.0, the app's version); peerDependencies become a permissive range so consumers on any 2.x still resolve a single framework copy.

Not decided here: whether to keep a compatibility floor at 2.16.0 in peerDependencies or raise it to 2.18.0. Default to the floor at 2.16.0 unless something in the 2.16->2.18 diff makes that a lie.
acceptance_criteria:
- peerDependencies accept 2.18.0; 'pnpm why @medusajs/framework' in the b2b app shows exactly ONE resolved version after install.
- yarn build, yarn lint, yarn test (L1) and the L2 full-app harness all pass against Medusa 2.18.0.
- The plugin can be installed into apps/backend by a command that also works on Medusa Cloud (registry install, or a git dep that builds via 'prepare').
- Plugin builds under Node 24; engines field reflects the supported range.

title: Fulfillment provider cannot resolve 'ongoing' module in a real Medusa app (module isolation) — createFulfillment/cancelFulfillment throw AwilixResolutionError
description:
EXPOSED BY the wh5.9 in-process full-app harness (integration-tests/full-app.spec.ts + full-app-fixture/), the first test to drive the provider through the REAL core FulfillmentModuleService instead of a hand-built container.

ACTUAL: In a booted full Medusa app, core FulfillmentModuleService.createFulfillment -> OngoingFulfillmentProviderService.createFulfillment throws 'AwilixResolutionError: Could not resolve ''ongoing''' at the integration lookup (src/providers/ongoing-fulfillment/service.ts). cancelFulfillment's diagnostic lookup has the same issue. So the plugin's CORE order-push path is broken in any real consuming app.

ROOT CAUSE: @medusajs/fulfillment/dist/loaders/providers.js registers each provider into the FULFILLMENT MODULE's own isolated container via asFunction((cradle) => new klass(cradle, options)). By Medusa module isolation, that container does NOT have sibling modules ('ongoing') or app-scope services ('query', the workflow engine) registered. The provider stores this cradle as this.container_ and (a) resolves the 'ongoing' module for getIntegrationByLocation and (b) runs the pushOrderToOngoing/pushReturnOrderToOngoing/cancelOngoingOrder workflows with it — none of which are resolvable from a module-isolated container. The existing unit/module specs masked this by injecting a fake container that has 'ongoing' registered (and a callable .resolve()); a real app has neither.

Two layers found:
1) cradle-vs-container: this.container_ is the awilix cradle (no .resolve()). Partial fix already drafted (read module via cradle property with a .resolve() fallback for the mocked tests) — necessary but INSUFFICIENT.
2) module isolation (the real bug): even via cradle property, 'ongoing' is not in the fulfillment module container.

LIKELY FIX (architectural, needs design): move the cross-module orchestration OUT of the provider's synchronous createFulfillment into an APP-SCOPE seam that can resolve all modules + run workflows — e.g. a subscriber on the fulfillment/delivery-created event (app container), mirroring how the ShipStation example triggers cross-module work. Provider methods should stay within what a module-isolated container can do. Re-verify with the wh5.9 full-app harness once fixed (it already reproduces this).

title: Fable agent audit: analyze plugin against Ongoing/Medusa WMS integration best practices
description:
## Why

The plugin has grown through many milestones (provider, workflows, subscribers, jobs, sync). We have never done a holistic, outside-in audit comparing our architecture and flows against (a) Ongoing Warehouse's own recommended integration patterns, (b) Medusa's official guidance on third-party/WMS integrations, and (c) how mature community Medusa fulfillment/IMS plugins structure the same concerns. This issue commissions that audit from a Fable-powered agent.

## What to do

Run this as a Fable model agent (claude-fable-5) with the `medusa-dev:building-with-medusa` skill loaded. The agent must:

1. **Read and understand the whole plugin** — src/providers, src/modules, src/workflows, src/subscribers, src/jobs, src/api, src/links, plus graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md (and graphify-out/wiki/index.md if present) for structure.

2. **Read and understand these required resources** (fetch them, don't rely on training data):
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/webshop-flow — Ongoing's canonical webshop order flow
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/inventory — inventory sync guidance
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/paginating-responses
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/parallel-requests — rate limiting/concurrency rules
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/integrate-transport-system
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/REST/v1/openapi.json?version=57 — API surface we should be using
   - https://github.com/Epic-Design-Labs/medusa-plugin-foundry-ims — comparable IMS plugin
   - https://github.com/pevey/medusa-plugins — community plugin patterns
   - https://github.com/medusajs/examples/tree/main/shipstation-integration — closest architectural model
   - https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/integrations/guides/shipstation
   - https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/best-practices/third-party-sync — Medusa's third-party sync best practices
   - https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/medusa-workflows-reference
   - https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/fulfillment

3. **Research beyond the list**: search online for additional authoritative resources that should inform the audit — e.g. Ongoing developer docs pages not listed above (webhooks/automation triggers, article/order status models), Medusa docs on inventory module, event bus, scheduled jobs, workflow compensation/retry patterns, idempotency in integrations, and other production Medusa WMS/3PL integrations (e.g. other 3PL plugins on npm/GitHub). Incorporate what's relevant and cite it.

4. **Compare and analyze** across at least these dimensions:
   - Order push flow vs Ongoing's recommended webshop flow (statuses, when to send, cancellation/edit windows, idempotency)
   - Inventory sync direction/cadence vs Ongoing inventory guidance and Medusa third-party-sync best practices
   - Fulfillment provider contract completeness vs Medusa fulfillment module reference (options, validation, cancellation, returns, tracking)
   - Workflow design: compensation, retries, error propagation, long-running sync patterns
   - Rate limiting/pagination/parallel-request compliance with Ongoing's rules
   - Webhook vs polling strategy vs what Ongoing supports
   - Module isolation, links, and data-model choices vs Medusa conventions and the reference plugins
   - Gaps: features similar plugins have that we lack (or intentionally skip — note why if discernible)

## Deliverables

1. **A written report** committed nowhere — attach as the issue's notes or a linked markdown in the issue comments (`bd comments`), structured as: executive summary, per-dimension findings (what we do / what best practice says / verdict / evidence with links), and a prioritized recommendation list.
2. **Actionable beads issues filed** (`bd create`) for every concrete, worthwhile change the audit surfaces — each with type, priority, description referencing the report finding and the source resource, and dependencies between them where ordering matters. Link them to this issue (use this issue as parent or reference its ID in descriptions).
3. Purely informational findings (no action needed) stay in the report only.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 13 required resources above were actually fetched and reflected in the report (each cited at least once or explicitly marked not-applicable)
- At least one round of independent online research beyond the given list, with sources cited
- Report covers all 8 comparison dimensions
- Every actionable recommendation has a corresponding filed bead with priority and rationale
- Report attached to this issue via bd comments/notes

AUDIT COMPLETE. Report: docs/audits/2026-07-15-s1k-wms-integration-audit.md

BUT the Ongoing HTTP client was never verified against the real REST spec — machine inspection of openapi.json v57 confirms: (C1/P0) pagination uses page/pageSize params that don't exist -> identical repeated requests, infinite loop when result >=50 rows (ji6); (C2/P0) GET /articles/inventory endpoint doesn't exist -> stock-sync 404s every tick (dtw); (C3/P1) tracking extraction reads parcels[].parcelTracking.code, real shape is parcels[].tracking.waybill -> poll-path tracking always empty (5vu). Also: throttle is per-client-instance so Ongoing's sequential-per-goods-owner rule isn't enforced process-wide (4s4); stockInfoChangedFrom delta sync unused (sw8); no article sync (sci); no wayOfDelivery mapping (rzd); N+1 inventory reconcile (3e8); webhook underused for status refresh (jzm); minor arch-workflow-required deviation in status-poll job (o6c); returns stubbed (9ah); stale graphify/CLAUDE.md (de5). title: order-updated.ts take:1 order_change query silently drops address/contact changes when bundled with other field edits
description:
Surfaced by whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (CRIT-4, adversarially confirmed). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## File
`src/subscribers/order-updated.ts:44-73`

## Failure scenario

Admin edits `shipping_address` AND `locale` (or any address/contact field bundled with `metadata`/`locale`) in the same `updateOrderWorkflow` call. Medusa's `updateOrderWorkflow` (`node_modules/@medusajs/core-flows/dist/order/workflows/update-order.js:125-193`) builds a `changes` array pushing one object per changed field, then passes the whole array to `registerOrderChangesStep` → `OrderModuleService.registerOrderChange_` (`node_modules/@medusajs/order/dist/services/order-module-service.js:1223-1242`).

That module service does `orderChangeService_.create(inputData.map(...))` — **one order_change DB row per array entry**, each with a single-element `actions` array. All rows share the same `created_at` timestamp (or microsecond-close), and address types are always pushed earlier in the array than locale/metadata.

The subscriber's query `pagination: { take: 1, order: { created_at: 'DESC' } }` returns whichever row the DB picks — non-deterministic across the group. When the returned row is `locale`, `hasAddressContactChange` evaluates false → Ongoing is never re-synced for a real address change.

## Why the tests missed this

The unit test in `src/subscribers/__tests__/order-updated.test.ts:42-56` mocks all detail types on a single synthetic order_change row with multiple `actions`. That does not match the real one-row-per-change shape that `registerOrderChange_` produces.

## Recommended fix

Query all order_change rows for this `order_id`/`change_type` since the last processed watermark (or within the same instant as the newest row), union their detail types, and derive `changedTypes` from the union — not from a single row.

## Verification (from review)

Refute pass verified against actual Medusa v2.16.0 source under node_modules — confirmed one-row-per-change semantics; confirmed `order.updated` fires once per updateOrders call, not per field; confirmed the change_type filter does not narrow to one row per type.

title: cancelFulfillment silently succeeds when it decides Ongoing shouldn't cancel — Medusa marks fulfillment cancelled while Ongoing keeps shipping
description:
Surfaced by whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (CRIT-3, adversarially confirmed). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## Files
- `src/providers/ongoing-fulfillment/service.ts:284` (main path)
- `src/providers/ongoing-fulfillment/service.ts:265` (no-identifier sub-case)

## Failure scenario

Order's Ongoing status has moved past the integration's `cancellable_status_codes`. `decideOngoingCancelStep` returns `{ shouldCancel: false, reason: 'status_not_cancellable' }`. Provider's `cancelFulfillment` returns `{ canceled: false, reason: 'status_not_cancellable' }` **without throwing**.

Medusa's core `FulfillmentModuleService.cancelFulfillment` (verified at `node_modules/@medusajs/fulfillment/dist/services/fulfillment-module-service.js:711-728`) only inspects throw/no-throw; on non-throw it unconditionally sets `fulfillment.canceled_at`. Result: Medusa shows the fulfillment as cancelled while Ongoing continues to pick, pack, and ship. The merchant believes the order was stopped; it wasn't.

Sub-case at line 265: when the fulfillment's stashed `data` lacks all three identifiers (`ongoing_order_number` / `medusa_fulfillment_id` / `medusa_order_id`), the provider also returns without throwing — same silent-mark-cancelled outcome even though no cancel request was ever sent.

## Plan-doc note

The plan for issue #22 lumped `status_not_cancellable` under "benign/idempotent" alongside `already_cancelled`. But those two have **opposite** real-world consequences: `already_cancelled` is a true no-op (Ongoing already stopped); `status_not_cancellable` isn't (Ongoing keeps shipping).

## Recommended fix

Throw a `MedusaError` (with a distinct type, e.g. `NOT_ALLOWED` or `INVALID_STATE`) for non-idempotent no-cancel outcomes so Medusa preserves the fulfillment's un-cancelled state. Only truly-idempotent successes (already cancelled) may resolve.

## Verification (from review)

Refute pass reviewed:
- Core Medusa module-service.js source: confirmed unconditional `canceled_at` set on any non-throw.
- The `order.canceled` subscriber independently re-runs `cancelOngoingOrderWorkflow`, but its ONGOING_EVENTS.ORDER_CANCELLED emit is gated on `shouldCancel === true`, so external event consumers aren't misled — but Medusa's own `fulfillment.canceled_at` field is wrong.
- No compensating mechanism found; no UI surfaces the mismatch.

title: putOrder returns { ongoingOrderId: undefined } when Ongoing's 2xx body omits orderId
description:
Surfaced by whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (CRIT-2, adversarially confirmed). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## File
`src/lib/ongoing/client.ts:115`

## Failure scenario

Ongoing returns 2xx without `orderId` in the body (async-accepted, empty 200, unexpected shape). `res.orderId` is `undefined`, but the return type declares `ongoingOrderId: number`, so TypeScript lets it through.

Callers persist the undefined:
- `src/workflows/steps/push-order-record-sync.ts:54-55,100`
- `src/workflows/steps/upsert-ongoing-order-edit.ts:73-88`

Both assign `res.ongoingOrderId` straight into a variable persisted via `recordSync({..., ongoing_order_id: ongoingOrderId})` with no null/undefined check. All future cancel/status/tracking lookups for that order permanently fail with no error trail.

## Compare

`cancelOrder` already defensively does `res?.orderId ?? ongoingOrderId` — the pattern exists in the same file, applied inconsistently.

## Recommended fix

Add the same defensive fallback + explicit error throw when the field is missing, or run a lightweight runtime schema validation on the response. Prefer the throw path so a missing orderId is surfaced, not silently persisted.

## Note

Real-world probability depends on Ongoing's actual API contract (not verified in this review). The code gap is real and unmitigated regardless.

title: client.ts safeJson + unchecked cast lets malformed 2xx bodies flow into the domain
description:
Surfaced by whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (CRIT-1, adversarially confirmed). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## Files
- `src/lib/ongoing/client.ts:71` (safeJson)
- `src/lib/ongoing/client.ts:84` (doFetch's `return parsed as T`)

## Failure scenario

Ongoing (or an intermediary proxy) returns HTTP 200 with a non-JSON body — HTML error page, truncated response, gateway timeout page. `safeJson` catches `JSON.parse`'s throw and returns the raw text string; `doFetch` casts the string to `T` with no content-type or shape validation. `putOrder` then reads `res.orderId` on a string, gets `undefined`, and returns `{ ongoingOrderId: undefined }` without ever surfacing an error. Downstream persistence writes an undefined into `OngoingOrderSync.ongoing_order_id` and every future cancel/tracking lookup permanently breaks with no error trail.

All other Ongoing operations flow through the same `doFetch` — this is the root of every downstream type-hole finding in the review.

## Recommended fix

- Validate `Content-Type: application/json` on the response before parsing.
- Throw a typed `OngoingApiError({ kind: 'terminal', reason: 'unexpected_body_shape' })` on mismatch.
- Do not swallow `JSON.parse` failures in `safeJson`.

## Verification (from review)

Verified by adversarial refute pass — confirmed no content-type or shape validation anywhere in `doFetch`; no test constructs a 200 response with malformed/non-JSON text; cancelOrder's `res?.orderId ?? ongoingOrderId` fallback is a symptom of the same gap, not a fix.

title: One command to update this plugin in a linked local Medusa app, including stale-copy cleanup
description:
Updating a linked app is currently a four-step ritual with two silent failure modes, and it cost a full debugging round on 2026-08-07 (see the pnpm section of docs/wiki/Dev-Local-App-Testing.md).

The steps: yarn build -> yalc publish --push -> the app package managers install -> restart the right dev server. What goes wrong:

- "npx medusa plugin:publish" does NOT push (it calls yalc publishPackage without --push), so it looks like it worked and the app keeps running the old build.
- In a pnpm app the push only overwrites the plain directory under the apps node_modules; pnpms virtual-store copy (node_modules/.pnpm/<pkg>@file+...) stays stale, the workspace-root symlink still points at it, and pnpm shoves its own copy into node_modules/.ignored. Up to four copies exist and only one is fresh.
- Nothing distinguishes builds: the version is 0.0.1 forever, so the only reliable check today is grepping node_modules for a string you just wrote.

Wanted: a script in this repo (e.g. scripts/push-to-local-app.mjs behind a "yarn push:local [app-path]") that does the whole update and proves it:

1. Build, then yalc publish --push.
2. Detect the target apps package manager (pnpm/yarn/npm, workspace or not) and run the right install from the package that actually depends on the plugin — not the workspace root.
3. Clean up stale copies: prune leftover .pnpm store entries for this package, remove node_modules/.ignored shadows, and drop the apps admin/vite caches so the admin bundle is rebuilt.
4. Verify: assert every reachable copy under the app carries the build marker from step 1 (see the build-stamp bead), and fail loudly listing the paths that do not.
5. Print which dev-server process holds which port, so the operator restarts the one they are browsing.

Linked apps are discoverable from "yalc installations show", so the script can operate on all linked apps or a named one. This stays a plugin-repo dev tool — nothing is written into the consuming apps repo beyond what the link already does.
design: Prefer a plain node script over adding a dependency. yalc is already available via node_modules/.bin/yalc in this repo. Package-manager detection from the app's lockfile; workspace root from pnpm-workspace.yaml / workspaces field.
acceptance_criteria: A single command updates a linked pnpm-workspace app end to end and exits non-zero if any reachable copy is stale; stale .pnpm/.ignored copies and the app's admin cache are cleaned; docs/wiki/Dev-Local-App-Testing.md points at the command instead of the manual four-step recipe.

title: precise reconcile mode adds back reservations of UNFULFILLED items on partially fulfilled orders (availability overstated)
description:
Why: in reconcile-inventory-levels.ts Batch 3 (lines ~113-133), precise mode collects synced line-item ids by listing OngoingOrderSyncs with sync_state='sent' and then taking ALL items of each matched order (query.graph entity 'order', fields ['id','items.id']). The ledger row is per (order, fulfillment) and a push happens per fulfillment, so on a partially fulfilled order the not-yet-fulfilled items are wrongly counted as 'synced': their reservations (which still exist — reservations are deleted only at fulfillment creation) are added back into stocked_quantity, so Medusa availability = sellable - reserved + wrongly_added_back overstates by the unfulfilled items' reserved qty. Ongoing knows nothing about those items (never pushed), so nothing offsets them.

Failure scenario: order with line A (qty 2, fulfilled -> pushed, sync row 'sent', reservation deleted) and line B (qty 3, unfulfilled, reservation live). Precise: syncedLineItemIds includes B; M_res_synced = 3; stocked = sellable + 3; available = sellable — but truth is sellable - 3.

Fix: scope to items on SENT FULFILLMENTS, not sent orders — use the sync row's medusa_fulfillment_id and query the fulfillment's items' line_item_id (order-sync<->fulfillment link is 1:1) instead of order.items.id. Note: after the corrected reservation-lifecycle analysis (see the 'sellable' mode bead), correctly-scoped precise yields M_res_synced ≈ 0 in the standard flow (fulfilled items have no reservations), which is consistent — and is an argument in that bead's open question about deprecating precise rather than fixing it; resolve the two together.

Add unit tests: partial-fulfillment case in steps/__tests__/reconcile-inventory-levels.test.ts pinning that only sent-fulfillment items' reservations are added back.
acceptance_criteria: Precise mode scopes reservation add-back to line items of sent fulfillments (or the mode is deprecated per the sellable-mode bead's decision); partial-fulfillment unit test pins the behavior.

title: Add a plain 'sellable' stock-reconcile mode; re-evaluate sellable_plus_reserved's min() add-back (availability overstated)
description:
Why: research into a proposed 'sellable + reserved minus Ongoing-vs-Medusa reservation diff' mode (2026-08-07), verified against both Medusa and Ongoing docs online, found that the correct implementation of the underlying goal is simpler than any of the existing add-back modes — and that the current default mode overstates availability.

Verified lifecycle facts:
(1) Medusa: createOrderFulfillmentWorkflow runs adjustInventoryLevelsStep + updateReservationsStep + deleteReservationsStep — at FULFILLMENT creation the reserved qty is subtracted from stocked_quantity and the reservation items are deleted (docs.medusajs.com/resources/references/medusa-workflows/createOrderFulfillmentWorkflow, /resources/commerce-modules/inventory/inventory-in-flows). Reservations exist only between order placement (completeCartWorkflow) and fulfillment creation.
(2) This plugin pushes the order to Ongoing at fulfillment creation (order.fulfillment_created subscriber -> pushOrderToOngoing; Dev-Architecture 'Order push' section).
(3) Ongoing: SellableNumberOfItems = NumberOfItems - LockedForSaleNumberOfItems - LeftToAllocate, LeftToAllocate = MAX(0, Ordered - Allocated), LockedForSale includes all allocations plus explicitly locked stock (developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/inventory) — i.e. sellable already excludes ALL open-order demand on the goods owner, from any channel.

Consequence: a unit is either 'reserved in Medusa, unknown to Ongoing' (pre-fulfillment) or 'in Ongoing, no Medusa reservation' (post-push) — the sets are DISJOINT. So sellable_plus_reserved's add-back min(medusa_reserved, ongoing_allocated) (reconcile-inventory-levels.ts:191-195) estimates an overlap that is actually zero, and Medusa availability is overstated by min(M_res, O_alloc) whenever unfulfilled reservations and pushed-not-yet-picked allocations coexist — an overselling window even with a single sales channel (e.g. the pinned test case sellable=14, alloc=3, M_res=2 -> stocked 16, available 14; truth is available 12). The 'so reservations don't double-deduct' rationale in the docs rests on the wrong assumption that Medusa reservations persist while the order sits allocated in Ongoing.

What to do:
1. FIRST verify the lifecycle empirically on the pinned Medusa version via the L2 full-app harness (integration-tests/full-app.spec.ts): place order -> reservation exists; create fulfillment with the Ongoing shipping option -> reservation deleted + stocked decremented. Gate the math change on this.
2. Add a 'sellable' value to stock_reconcile_mode: stocked = max(0, sellableNumberOfItems), incoming from toReceiveNumberOfItems unchanged. Medusa then derives available = sellable - reserved, which is exactly right: unfulfilled Medusa orders and manual Medusa reservations subtract once (Ongoing can't see them), and all Ongoing-side demand incl. other channels and locked stock is excluded inside sellable. This — not a diff-subtraction — is the correct realization of 'reservations done outside Medusa must not be treated as sellable in Medusa'.
3. Touch points: enum in src/modules/ongoing/models/integration.ts (+ migration via plugin:db:generate — see memory 'plugin-db-generate-recipe'), zod validators in src/api/admin/ongoing/integrations/validators.ts and [id]/validators.ts, mode types in src/workflows/sync-ongoing-inventory.ts + steps/reconcile-inventory-levels.ts, branch in the step, admin select options + help copy in src/admin/routes/settings/ongoing/integration-form-fields.tsx (file currently has uncommitted changes — coordinate), unit tests in steps/__tests__/reconcile-inventory-levels.test.ts.
4. Product decision (flag with bd human if needed): make 'sellable' the default for new integrations? Deprecate or keep sellable_plus_reserved (silently changing its formula would alter behavior for existing installs; an explicit new mode + docs is cleaner). Also decide the fate of 'precise' — after the lifecycle correction it approximates stocked=sellable in the standard flow and mainly differs via its partial-fulfillment scoping bug (separate bead).
5. Do NOT implement the originally proposed diff-subtraction (stocked = sellable + M_res - (O_alloc - M_res)): sellable already excludes allocations, so it double-deducts external demand (onhand 20, external order 3, no reservations -> proposed 14, truth 17), and an aggregate diff is unattributable (M_res > O_alloc is benign unfulfilled demand; O_alloc drops at pick while nothing corresponds in Medusa).
acceptance_criteria: L2 evidence that reservations are deleted at fulfillment creation on the pinned Medusa version; 'sellable' mode selectable end-to-end (model+migration+validators+workflow+admin form) and covered by unit tests; default-mode decision recorded; docs bead unblocked.
notes: Origin: user proposal for a reservation-diff reconcile mode; assessment 2026-08-07 with medusa-dev:building-with-medusa loaded, Medusa + Ongoing docs checked online. Supersedes the analysis portion of MedusaOngoingWarehousePlugin-dt0's original description.

title: Docs: explain stock-reconcile-mode choice for multi-channel warehouses (external Ongoing orders)
description:
Why: research into a proposed fourth reconcile mode ('sellable + reserved, minus the diff between Ongoing allocated and Medusa reserved') concluded it must NOT be implemented — Ongoing's SellableNumberOfItems is defined as NumberOfItems - LockedForSaleNumberOfItems - LeftToAllocate (see developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/inventory), so ALL open-order demand on the goods owner (allocated + not-yet-allocated + locked stock, from any channel) is already excluded from sellable. Subtracting an allocated-vs-reserved diff on top would deduct external orders a second time and systematically understate Medusa availability (e.g. onhand 20, external order 3, no Medusa reservations: sellable=17, proposed stocked=14).

The underlying concern is real though, and the docs don't address it: in the default sellable_plus_reserved mode, the min(medusa_reserved, ongoing_allocated) add-back cannot tell Medusa-pushed allocations from external-channel allocations. When unpushed Medusa reservations (order placed, fulfillment not yet created) coexist with external allocations on the same goods owner, Medusa availability is overstated by up to min(unpushed_reservations, external_allocations) — an overselling window. 'precise' mode already fixes exactly this by adding back only reservations attributable to orders with sync_state='sent' (available = sellable - unpushed Medusa reservations; external demand excluded via sellable itself).

What to do: extend the 'Stock reconcile modes' section of docs/wiki/User-Configuration-Reference.md (and the matching inline help copy in src/admin/routes/settings/ongoing/integration-form-fields.tsx — the docs page says the two must stay in sync) to explain: (1) when each mode is appropriate, (2) that warehouses where OTHER channels also order against the same Ongoing goods owner should use 'precise', (3) the default mode's mis-attribution window and its bound, (4) that sellable already excludes all open-order demand, so no mode should ever re-subtract Ongoing allocations. Mention it in User-How-It-Works if the inventory-sync section exists there.
acceptance_criteria: User-Configuration-Reference.md reconcile-modes section explains the multi-channel scenario and recommends precise for it; admin form help copy for stock_reconcile_mode updated in sync; no code changes.
notes: CORRECTION (2026-08-07, after checking Medusa docs online with building-with-medusa loaded): the original description's claim that reservations persist until shipment is WRONG — createOrderFulfillmentWorkflow deletes reservations and decrements stocked_quantity at FULFILLMENT creation, i.e. exactly when this plugin pushes to Ongoing. So Medusa reservations and Ongoing allocations are disjoint sets, the default mode's min() add-back estimates an overlap that is actually zero (availability overstated by min(M_res, O_alloc) even single-channel), and 'precise' is NOT exactly correct (partial-fulfillment scoping bug, bead v7a). Write these docs AFTER the mode work in bead 8i2 lands, reflecting whatever modes/default come out of it. Still valid from the original analysis: Ongoing's SellableNumberOfItems = NumberOfItems - LockedForSaleNumberOfItems - LeftToAllocate (verified verbatim), so sellable already excludes ALL open-order demand incl. other channels, and the proposed diff-subtraction mode must not be implemented (double-deducts external demand; aggregate diff unattributable).

title: Status code pickers: explain what each of the three lists drives
description:
src/admin/routes/settings/ongoing/components/StatusCodePicker.tsx and its three usages in integration-form-fields.tsx

Shipped / Delivered / Cancellable status codes render as a bare label over a checkbox list. The empty-state copy (run Test connection to load statuses) is good, but nothing says what selecting a code actually causes:

- Shipped status codes: which Ongoing statuses mean the order has shipped, i.e. which ones make the status poll and the webhook mark the Medusa fulfillment as shipped and pull tracking.
- Delivered status codes: same, for delivery.
- Cancellable status codes: which Ongoing statuses still allow a cancel to be pushed — and that cancelling an order sitting outside this list will fail.

Also worth surfacing: leaving a list empty means that transition never fires, and the codes are tenant-specific (the sandbox map in the bd memory ongoing-live-sandbox-tenant... shows 200 Aapen through 1000 Annullert), so there is no universally correct selection — the operator must pick from their own Ongoing setup.

StatusCodePicker takes a label prop only; add an optional description/hint prop rather than duplicating copy at each call site.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three pickers has a description of what selecting a code causes; empty-list consequence stated; StatusCodePicker gained a description prop rather than three copies of the markup.
close_reason: StatusCodePicker gained an optional description prop; the three call sites now explain what each list drives. Correction to the bead's premise: an empty shipped/delivered list does NOT disable the transition — resolveShipmentStage falls back to canonical codes (425/450/451 and 500), and delivered is checked first. Only cancellable has no fallback: empty => every cancel on a known status is refused. Copy says exactly this.

title: Stock reconcile mode: label the options in plain language instead of raw enum values

src/admin/routes/settings/ongoing/integration-form-fields.tsx

title: Help text for the Enabled and Stock sync enabled switches
description:
src/admin/routes/settings/ongoing/integration-form-fields.tsx

Two bare Label + Switch rows with no description:

- Enabled: does not say what turns off. Should state that disabling stops order pushes, status polling, and stock sync for this warehouse, that in-flight sync rows are left alone, and that it is the safe way to pause an integration without deleting it (deleting is separate and leaves setup artifacts behind).

title: Help text and unit clarity for the two interval fields (stock sync, status poll)
description:
src/admin/routes/settings/ongoing/integration-form-fields.tsx

Stock sync interval (ms) and Status poll interval (ms) are plain text Inputs with only a placeholder (e.g. 300000 / e.g. 60000). Problems an operator hits:

- No statement of what happens when the field is empty — it falls back to the plugin-level defaultStockSyncInterval / defaultStatusPollInterval, and then to the built-in default. The form should say the fallback chain and the effective default value.
- Milliseconds are an awkward unit to type; 300000 vs 30000 is a silent order-of-magnitude mistake. At minimum add a hint that renders the humanised equivalent, or state the sensible range.
- No stated minimum. The cron jobs run on a fixed schedule (stock sync and status poll every 15 min, retry sweep every 5 min per CLAUDE.md), so an interval far below the cron tick does nothing. Say so, and say the Ongoing rate limits make aggressive values counterproductive.
- The field accepts any string with no validation feedback; a non-numeric value is only rejected server-side, if at all. Check what the create/update route validates and state the accepted format.

Confirm the actual fallback chain and defaults in src/modules/ongoing/options.ts and the jobs before writing the copy.
acceptance_criteria: Both interval fields state unit, effective default when empty, the fallback chain, and a sensible range; copy verified against options.ts and the jobs.
close_reason: Interval hints state ms unit with humanised examples, the blank->defaultStockSyncInterval(600000)/defaultStatusPollInterval(60000) fallback chain, that both cron jobs tick every 15 min so <900000 means 'every tick', and that a non-numeric value is ignored (route only type-checks string; resolveIntervalMs falls back). Placeholders changed to realistic values.

The operator has no way to know these come from the plugin options in medusa-config (the integrations array), that the list is not editable from the UI, and that the key is immutable after creation. - Goods owner id (Input, number): already has a description, but it does not say the value is the numeric goodsOwnerId from Ongoing, where to find it in the Ongoing UI, or that Test connection is the way to confirm the pair is valid before saving. title: Per-sales-channel Ongoing order class, sent on pushed orders
description:
Orders pushed to Ongoing should carry an order class that depends on which Medusa sales channel the order came from, so the warehouse can route/prioritise/label per channel (e.g. B2B vs webshop vs marketplace).

WHAT ONGOING EXPECTS (verified against OpenAPI v57, 2026-08-06):
- `PostOrderModel.classes` is an ARRAY of `PostOrderClass { code?, name?, comment?, isParcelTypeSuggestion? }` — order classes are a list, not a single value, so the mapping must be sales channel -> one or more class codes.
- Available classes for a goods owner can be listed with `GET /api/v1/orders/classes` (`GetOrderClassesModel.orderClasses[] { code, name, comment }`) — useful for validating configured codes and for an admin picker.
- Post-push mutation endpoints exist (`PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/setOrderClasses`, `/addOrderClasses`, `DELETE .../classes`) — OUT OF SCOPE here; this bead only stamps classes at push time.
- `PostOrderModel` is `additionalProperties: false`, so the key must be exactly `classes`.

WHAT IS MISSING TODAY:
- `PostOrderModel` in src/lib/ongoing/types.ts has no `classes` field, and src/lib/ongoing/order-mapper.ts never emits one.
- `MapOrderInput` carries no channel/class data, and src/workflows/steps/map-order-to-ongoing.ts has nothing to map from.
- src/lib/ongoing/re-query-fulfillment-order.ts does not select `order.sales_channel_id` (or `order.sales_channel.name`), so the channel is not even loaded on the push path.
- There is no configuration surface anywhere for a channel -> class mapping (grep for sales_channel across src/ and docs/wiki returns nothing).

SCOPE:
1. Config: persist the mapping per integration (see design).
2. Query: add the sales channel to the fulfillment/order graph query.
3. Map: thread it into `MapOrderInput` and emit `classes` from the pure mapper (drop silently when unmapped — an unmapped channel must never block a push).
4. Admin: expose the mapping in the Ongoing settings UI alongside the other per-integration rules.
5. Docs: update docs/wiki (configuration reference + the order-push flow page) in the same PR.
design:
RECOMMENDED SHAPE (open to change during implementation):

- Store the mapping in the DB on `OngoingIntegration` as a nullable json column, e.g. `order_class_rules`, following the existing `edit_sync_rules` / `shipped_status_codes` precedent. Rationale: plugin options hold credentials only and are not admin-editable; per-integration operational config already lives on this model and is edited from the settings UI. Requires `npx medusa plugin:db:generate` + a migration.
- Suggested value shape: `{ "default": ["WEB"], "by_sales_channel": { "sc_123": ["B2B", "PRIO"] } }` — array-valued because Ongoing takes a list; an optional `default` covers orders whose channel is unmapped (or is absent). Keep the resolution helper pure and unit-testable, mirroring src/lib/ongoing/way-of-delivery.ts: a LENIENT extractor used at push time (malformed config -> no classes, order still pushes) plus a STRICT validator used when the admin saves the mapping.
- Emit only `code` (and `name` when configured). Do not send `isParcelTypeSuggestion` unless a concrete need appears.
- Alternatives considered: (a) sales-channel `metadata` — no admin UI, easy to typo, invisible in the Ongoing settings page; (b) plugin options in medusa-config — requires a redeploy to change a class and mixes ops config with credentials. Both rejected in favour of the DB column, but the choice is worth a sanity check with Thomas before building the admin form.

Not decided: whether to validate configured codes against `GET /api/v1/orders/classes` on save (nice, catches typos, but adds a live API call to the settings save path) or just accept free-text codes. Default to free-text + a non-blocking 'unknown code' warning in the admin UI if the class list is cheap to fetch.
acceptance_criteria:
- `PostOrderModel.classes` exists in src/lib/ongoing/types.ts matching the OpenAPI v57 `PostOrderClass` shape.
- The pure mapper emits `classes` when the resolved order class list is non-empty and omits the key entirely when it is empty/unmapped; covered by unit tests for both branches plus malformed config.
- The push path loads the order's sales channel and resolves classes from the integration's configured mapping; an order in an unmapped channel still pushes successfully (no class, no error).
- Per-integration mapping is persisted (model column + generated migration) and editable from the Ongoing settings admin UI.
- L1 unit suite green; `yarn lint` and `yarn build` clean.
- docs/wiki configuration reference and the order-push documentation describe the mapping and its value shape.
notes:
Filed 2026-08-06 from a request by Thomas. Field names verified against https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/REST/v1/openapi.json?version=57 during filing — re-verify if the spec version moves.

Touch points: src/lib/ongoing/types.ts, src/lib/ongoing/order-mapper.ts, src/lib/ongoing/re-query-fulfillment-order.ts (add `order.sales_channel_id` / `order.sales_channel.name`), src/workflows/steps/map-order-to-ongoing.ts, src/modules/ongoing/models/integration.ts, src/api/admin/ongoing/*, src/admin/ (settings page), docs/wiki/.

Related: return orders go through src/lib/ongoing/return-order-mapper.ts — decide whether returns should carry classes too (probably not; Ongoing return orders are a different model).

title: Name every when() branch in the workflows — Medusa 2.18 warns that random names are unsafe for production
description:
Surfaced while verifying the plugin against Medusa 2.18.0 (bead 9y2.1). 2.18 emits a new warning for every unnamed when() branch:

  '<workflow>: "when" name should be defined. A random one will be assigned to it, which is not recommended for production.'

There are 18 when( call sites under src/workflows (cleanup-location is the noisiest, e.g. cleanup-location.ts:149 and :190). A randomly-assigned name means the step identity is not stable across process restarts, which is exactly what the workflow engine keys retries and idempotency on — so this is a correctness risk for long-running/retried workflows, not only log noise.

Fix: pass an explicit stable name to each when(), following whatever the 2.18 signature is (name argument or options object — check the workflows-sdk source at node_modules/@medusajs/workflows-sdk/src/utils/composer/when.ts). Names must be stable forever once shipped, same constraint as step names.

Not urgent for the 9y2 install epic — the plugin builds, lints and passes L1 (740/740) and L2 (51/51) on 2.18.0 with these warnings present. But it should land before the plugin runs production traffic in the b2b app.
acceptance_criteria:
- No 'when name should be defined' warnings in the L2 integration run.
- Every when() branch has an explicit, stable name.
- L1 and L2 suites still green.

title: End-to-end round trip in the real app: admin UI, order push, status poll, stock sync, webhook
description:
The point of the whole epic — exercise the plugin as a human against a real B2B app, not a fixture.

- Admin UI: /ongoing dashboard, /settings/ongoing settings page, and the order-detail widget all render inside the b2b admin (which carries a lot of its own admin extensions — check for route or widget-zone collisions, and that @medusajs/ui 4.2.0 in the app does not break components built against 4.1.16).

- Order edit and cancellation: confirm the order-edit-confirmed / order-canceled subscribers drive the matching Ongoing sync.
- Status: let status-poll run (or trigger it) and confirm shipped/delivered interpretation and tracking extraction. NOTE from the sandbox: tracked orders sit at status 200 (Åpen) with waybill 'testWaybill', NOT in the shipped band — do not expect a shipped transition without moving the order in Ongoing.
- Stock: run stock-sync and confirm stocked_quantity reconciliation against the b2b catalog's real SKUs. Expect unmatched SKUs — the b2b catalog and the Ongoing sandbox are not the same product set. Capture that as data for the hhw epic rather than treating it as a failure.
- Webhook: hit /ongoing/webhooks/<credentialKey> with the static secret and confirm the status push is accepted and applied.
- Failure paths: confirm a failing push does NOT wedge fulfillment creation in the b2b app's own order flow (approvals, quotes, bookings all sit on top of it), and that retry-failed-syncs picks the row up.
- Log every real-app defect as its own bead rather than fixing inline.

- An order pushed to the Ongoing sandbox is visible there, with a 'synced' ledger row.

No core table altered. Re-run reports 'Database already up-to-date' with the count unchanged, so it is idempotent.
