title: Renaming a variant SKU silently breaks inbound stock sync (inventory item keeps the old SKU)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (from core-flows source; NOT yet reproduced against a running app):
Medusa copies the variant SKU onto the inventory item exactly once, at variant-creation time — @medusajs/core-flows/dist/product/workflows/create-product-variants.js:77 (sku: variantInput.sku). update-product-variants.js has NO sku propagation to the linked inventory item; it only reacts to manage_inventory === false. So after an operator edits a variant's SKU, the variant and its inventory item permanently disagree.

That divergence splits this plugin's two paths, because they read the SKU from different entities:
- OUTBOUND: resolveArticleNumber (src/lib/ongoing/resolve-article-number.ts:52) queries entity 'product_variant' by sku -> pushes the NEW sku to Ongoing as articleNumber, and ensureArticlesExist creates the article there.
- INBOUND: reconcileInventoryLevelsStep (src/workflows/steps/reconcile-inventory-levels.ts:85) calls listInventoryItems({ sku }) -> looks up INVENTORY ITEM sku, which is still the OLD value.

ACTUAL: after a SKU rename, orders keep pushing fine under the new articleNumber, but stock for that SKU never updates again. The Ongoing row matches 0 inventory items and takes the skip path (:163-169) — a single logger.warn, no operator-visible signal. Permanent, and silent.
EXPECTED: either the stock sync keeps matching after a rename, or the operator is told plainly that a rename orphaned the inventory item.

ENV: Medusa 2.16.0, this plugin on main @ 3857624.

Note this is not purely an Ongoing concern — a variant/inventory-item SKU divergence is a Medusa-level footgun. But this plugin is unusually exposed to it because it is the thing that reads inventory-item SKU on a 15-minute cron and reports success while matching nothing.

FIX DIRECTION (decide after repro, do not pre-commit):
(a) Detect and report — the cheapest, and it composes with hhw.3: when an Ongoing articleNumber matches 0 inventory items but DOES match a product_variant by sku, that is diagnostic proof of a rename orphan, and the message can say so instead of the generic 'matched 0 inventory items'.
(b) Match through the variant link instead of the inventory item's own sku — resolve variant by sku, then follow product_variant_inventory_item to the item. Makes inbound and outbound read the same authority. Larger change, and query.graph cannot filter across linked modules, so verify the query shape (query.index or query from the variant side) before committing.
(c) Repair — a maintenance action that rewrites the inventory item sku to match its variant. Mutating core inventory items from a fulfillment plugin needs care.

Option (a) is likely correct on its own: it costs one extra query only on the unmatched path, and it converts a silent permanent failure into a specific, actionable message.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reproduced on the L2 full-app harness (integration-tests/full-app.spec.ts): create variant with manage_inventory + SKU, rename the SKU, run the inventory sync, assert the level does NOT update and the row is counted unmatched.
- Root cause confirmed against the running app (not just source reading) before any patch.
- Chosen fix implemented with a minimal diff, no drive-by refactors.
- Regression test asserts the failure cannot return, citing this bead ID and the fix PR.
- Docs: the SKU-rename hazard is called out wherever the inventory-item prerequisite is documented (see MedusaOngoingWarehousePlugin-vm6).
notes: Repro harness: see the l2-full-app-harness bd memory for the exact invocation (env -u PGHOST -u DATABASE_URL, DB_HOST=localhost, --runInBand --forceExit). Related: MedusaOngoingWarehousePlugin-hhw.3 (unmatched reporting is where fix (a) would surface), MedusaOngoingWarehousePlugin-vm6 (docs). Verified in source: create-product-variants.js:77 copies sku at create; update-product-variants.js:111-117 handles only manage_inventory === false.

title: Surface stock-sync outcome counters and unmatched SKUs on the integration + dashboard
description:
Make the silent skips visible. Today the only evidence that a SKU never syncs is a logger.warn; an operator has no way to learn that 37 of their Ongoing articles have no Medusa variant.

Decision (confirmed): counters plus a bounded sample on the OngoingIntegration row, rendered in the dashboard. A dedicated unmatched-SKU model was rejected — unbounded growth, a migration, and a retention policy for data that is transient by nature.

Scope:
- OngoingIntegration (src/modules/ongoing/models/integration.ts): add last_stock_sync_stats as model.json().nullable() — a single column holding { written, created, updated, ignored, unmatched, collisions, unmatched_skus: string[] }. One JSON column rather than six scalar columns keeps the migration small and the shape evolvable.
- CAP unmatched_skus at ~50 entries and record the true total separately, so a catalogue-wide mismatch cannot bloat the row.
- Persist after a successful sync only, alongside the existing cursor advance (last_stock_delta_cursor / last_full_stock_sync_at), so a failed run does not overwrite the last good picture.
- Dashboard: extend the Connection Health panel on /ongoing to render the counts, with the unmatched sample behind a disclosure. Load medusa-dev:building-admin-dashboard-customizations before touching src/admin.
- Requires npx medusa plugin:db:generate (module model changed). See the plugin-db-generate-recipe memory: needs a live Postgres + DB_* vars.
- Distinguish ignored (expected: non-stock/inactive/kit, from hhw.1) from unmatched (actionable: a real stock-bearing article with no Medusa variant) from collisions (SKU matched >1 inventory item). Conflating them is what makes the current log useless.
acceptance_criteria:
- last_stock_sync_stats persists written/created/updated/ignored/unmatched/collisions plus a capped unmatched-SKU sample.
- Sample is capped (~50) and the true unmatched total is recorded independently of the sample length.
- Stats are written only on a successful sync; a failed run leaves the previous stats intact.
- Dashboard Connection Health shows the counts, and the unmatched sample is reachable without reading logs.
- Migration generated and committed.
- L1 tests cover the cap, the ignored/unmatched/collision split, and that a failed sync does not clobber prior stats.
notes: Deliberately NOT emitting a new ongoing.sync.inventory_unmatched event in this slice — the plugin already emits inventory_synced, and adding an alerting integration point can follow once the counters prove useful. Admin work: src/admin ops dashboard (/ongoing).

title: Auto-create missing inventory levels via batchInventoryItemLevelsWorkflow
description:
Turn skip-path 3 into a create. When an Ongoing article resolves to exactly one Medusa inventory item but that item has no inventory level at the integration's stock_location_id (reconcile-inventory-levels.ts:180-186), create the level instead of warning and skipping. This is the single most likely real-world cause of 'stock isn't syncing for some SKUs'.

Decision (confirmed): always create, no config flag. Ongoing reporting the article implies the goods are physically at that warehouse, and the integration's stock location IS that warehouse. An opt-in flag was rejected — everyone would enable it.

Creating LEVELS is safe; creating inventory ITEMS is not, and stays prohibited. A standalone inventory item has no product_variant_inventory_item link: unsellable, invisible on the product page, and it poisons future syncs by turning listInventoryItems({sku}) into the >1 collision path. Unmatched SKUs remain unmatched and get reported (sibling bead).

Scope:
- Restructure so the compute step is pure — resolve + classify + compute, returning { create: [], update: [], unmatched: [], ignored: [] } — and the writes go through batchInventoryItemLevelsWorkflow.runAsStep({ input: { create, update } }) in sync-ongoing-inventory.ts. One call does both halves, gives compensation for free, and brings the step in line with arch-workflow-required (the step currently resolves Modules.INVENTORY and calls updateInventoryLevels directly).
- Preserve the existing batching: one listInventoryItems, one listInventoryLevels, one listReservationItems, chunked writes (LEVEL_WRITE_CHUNK = 100).
- Keep the >1 SKU collision path as a skip. Medusa does not enforce unique SKU across inventory items, so never guess.
- Race tolerance: createInventoryLevelsStep runs validateInventoryLocationsStep (location exists) but does NOT dedupe against existing levels. Two overlapping syncs can both decide to create the same level; the unique-constraint violation must be treated as success, not a sync failure. Note the stock_sync_lock_until advisory lock already makes this unlikely but does not make it impossible.
acceptance_criteria:
- Item exists + no level at stock_location_id -> level is created with the computed stocked_quantity and incoming_quantity, in the same run (not deferred to the next tick).
- Item exists + level exists -> updated exactly as today; all three stock_reconcile_modes unchanged.
- SKU matches 0 items -> still no item created, reported as unmatched.
- SKU matches >1 items -> still skipped.
- Writes go through batchInventoryItemLevelsWorkflow, not a direct Modules.INVENTORY call in the step.
- Duplicate-level creation from a concurrent sync does not fail the run.
- Batching behavior preserved (assert call counts in tests, as the existing suite already does).
- L1 tests cover create, update, mixed create+update in one run, and the duplicate race.
notes: Core-flow refs: @medusajs/core-flows batchInventoryItemLevelsWorkflow (create/update/delete + force flag), createInventoryLevelsWorkflow, createInventoryItemsWorkflow (NOT to be used here). Existing tests to keep green: src/workflows/steps/__tests__/reconcile-inventory-levels.test.ts, src/workflows/__tests__/sync-ongoing-inventory.test.ts.

title: Classify Ongoing article rows (isStockArticle / isActive / articleKind) before SKU matching
description:
Foundation for the rest of the epic. Extend the inventory row schema and mapper to carry the article-classification fields Ongoing already returns, and partition the feed before it reaches SKU matching, so 'unmatched' means 'a real Medusa catalogue gap' instead of 'freight charge, discontinued article, or kit component'.

Ongoing's GET /articles returns the whole goods-owner article catalogue. Per the inventory docs, kit (structure) articles derive sellable qty as the min over their components, and the components are separate rows — neither kits nor components are reliably webshop products. Non-stock articles (services, freight, fees) carry meaningless inventory numbers. Without this classification, the unmatched list from the reporting slice would be dominated by rows nobody should act on, which trains operators to ignore it.

Scope:
- OngoingInventoryRowResponseSchema (src/lib/ongoing/schemas.ts:13): add isStockArticle, isActive, articleKind. Use .nullish() not .optional() — Ongoing serializes absent members as JSON null (bead dw5).
- OngoingInventoryRow (src/lib/ongoing/types.ts:20) + mapInventoryRow (client.ts): carry the fields through.
- reconcileInventoryLevelsStep: partition rows into ignored (isStockArticle === false, or isActive === false) vs candidates, BEFORE the listInventoryItems lookup. Count ignored separately from skipped.
- articleKind is a free-form string in the spec (not an enum) — do NOT hardcode a kit value blind. Verify actual values against the live sandbox first (see .env.integration / L3 harness) and treat unknown kinds as candidates rather than ignoring them.
acceptance_criteria:
- Schema parses isStockArticle/isActive/articleKind, tolerating null and absent.
- Rows with isStockArticle === false or isActive === false are classified ignored and never reach SKU matching.
- Ignored is reported as its own count, distinct from skipped/unmatched.
- Null/absent classification fields are treated as candidates (fail open — an older Ongoing tenant that omits them must not have its whole feed ignored).
- articleKind handling is based on values observed against the real sandbox, not guessed; unknown kinds fail open.
- L1 unit tests cover: non-stock ignored, inactive ignored, null fields fail open, ignored rows excluded from the unmatched count.
notes: Fail-open on null is the critical safety property here — a tenant whose API omits these fields must degrade to today's behavior, not to an empty sync. Live-verify articleKind via the L3 harness (yarn test:live, .env.integration) before assigning meaning to any value.

title: Inventory sync: classify the Ongoing article feed, auto-create missing levels, report unmatched SKUs
description:
Today the stock sync (sync-ongoing-inventory -> reconcileInventoryLevelsStep) is update-only and silently skips three cases: SKU matched 0 Medusa inventory items, SKU matched >1 (collision), and item exists but has no inventory level at the integration's stock_location_id. All three are logger.warn + skipped++ with no operator-visible signal.

Research (Ongoing OpenAPI v57 + developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/inventory + /webshop-flow) established the governing fact: **Ongoing's article catalogue is a superset of the webshop catalogue.** GetArticleModel carries isStockArticle (false for services/freight/fees), isActive (discontinued articles keep appearing), and articleKind/structure articles (kits, whose sellable qty is the min over components — components are themselves rows and are normally not webshop products). The plugin's zod schema stops at articleNumber + inventoryInfo, so it currently cannot distinguish an expected non-match from a real catalogue gap.

Medusa side: an inventory item created standalone (createInventoryItemsWorkflow) has no product_variant_inventory_item link — unsellable, invisible on product pages, and it turns the next sync's listInventoryItems({sku}) into the >1 collision path. Medusa creates inventory items FROM the variant (createProductVariantsWorkflow -> createInventoryItemsWorkflow + link when manage_inventory is true). Inventory-item identity is a catalogue concern; a WMS stock feed answers 'how many', never 'what do we sell'. This also matches what the plugin already enforces outbound: resolveArticleNumber requires a SKU to match exactly one Medusa variant or it throws terminal.

Agreed design (4 decisions, all confirmed with the user 2026-07-31):
1. ALWAYS auto-create a missing inventory LEVEL when the inventory item exists (no config flag).
2. NEVER auto-create inventory ITEMS from the stock feed.
3. Classify the feed client-side on isStockArticle/isActive/articleKind so 'unmatched' becomes a real signal; keep GET /articles (retains toReceiveNumberOfItems -> incoming_quantity).
4. Surface counters + a bounded sample of unmatched SKUs on the integration row and in the dashboard.

Rejected, with reasons recorded: opt-in flag for level creation (everyone would enable it); a dedicated unmatched-SKU model (unbounded growth + migration for transient data); switching to GET /articles/inventoryPerWarehouse (has excludeStructureArticles/excludeNonStockArticles server-side, but its model has no toReceiveNumberOfItems, so incoming_quantity sync would be lost) — filed separately; building an ERP-driven catalogue importer now (out of scope, separate epic).
acceptance_criteria:
- Stock sync auto-creates missing inventory levels and no longer silently skips that case.
- Non-stock / inactive / structure articles are classified as 'ignored', not counted as unmatched.
- Operators can see written / created / ignored / unmatched counts and a sample of unmatched SKUs without reading logs.
- No inventory items are ever created by the stock sync.
- docs/wiki pages reflect the new behavior and the inventory-item prerequisite.
- yarn lint, yarn build, yarn test clean.
notes: Endpoint comparison recorded for the follow-up epic — GET /articles: onlyArticlesInStock + isObsolete filters, HAS toReceiveNumberOfItems, aggregates across all warehouses. GET /articles/inventoryPerWarehouse: excludeStructureArticles + excludeNonStockArticles + warehouseIds filters, NO toReceiveNumberOfItems, per-warehouse. Both share stockInfoChangedFrom (24h cap) and articleSystemIdFrom cursor pagination. Current model is one goods owner -> one Medusa stock location receiving the cross-warehouse aggregate.

title: Docs: inventory-item prerequisites, SKU matching, and what the sync does/does not create
description:
The plugin's inventory sync (stock-sync job -> sync-ongoing-inventory -> reconcileInventoryLevelsStep) is UPDATE-ONLY. It resolves each Ongoing article to a Medusa inventory item by exact SKU match (listInventoryItems({sku})), then updates the pre-existing inventory LEVEL at the integration's stock location. It never calls createInventoryItems, never creates an inventory level, and never touches products/variants.

Three silent skip paths in src/workflows/steps/reconcile-inventory-levels.ts, each only a logger.warn + skipped++:
1. SKU matched 0 Medusa inventory items -> skipped
2. SKU matched >1 inventory items (collision) -> skipped
3. Item exists but has no inventory level at the integration's stock_location_id -> skipped

Operationally this means: if a merchant has articles in Ongoing that don't exist as Medusa product variants (with manage_inventory on, matching SKU, and a location level at the linked stock location), stock sync silently does nothing for them and only the skipped counter/log reveals it. The docs never say this. User-How-It-Works.md 'Inventory sync — Ongoing to Medusa' describes cursors and reconcile modes but not the matching contract; User-Verification.md's inventory check assumes 'a known SKU' already works; User-Setup-Guide.md lists no product/inventory prerequisite.

Note the asymmetry worth documenting: the OUTBOUND direction does auto-create — ensureArticlesExist() PUTs each order SKU as an Ongoing article before the order push. INBOUND does not. That asymmetry is exactly what makes the current docs misleading.
acceptance_criteria:
- User-How-It-Works.md inventory-sync section states explicitly that sync is update-only, matches by exact SKU, and requires a pre-existing inventory item + level at the linked stock location.
- Documents the three skip conditions (no match, SKU collision, no level at location) and what the operator sees (warn log + skipped count).
- Explains the Medusa side of the relationship: product variant -> inventory item (created by Medusa when manage_inventory is on) -> inventory level per stock location; and that the plugin creates none of these.
- User-Setup-Guide.md gains a prerequisite: SKUs and location levels must exist in Medusa before enabling stock sync.
- User-Troubleshooting.md gains a 'stock not updating for some SKUs' entry pointing at the skip warnings.
- User-Verification.md inventory check notes how to spot skipped rows.
- Documents the outbound/inbound asymmetry (Ongoing articles auto-created on push; Medusa inventory items never auto-created).

- Non-stock / inactive / structure articles are classified 'ignored', not 'unmatched' (hhw.1).
- Unmatched SKUs are visible as counters + a sample on the dashboard (hhw.3) — docs should point operators there, not at logs.
Also document: the variant -> inventory item -> level chain is created by Medusa when the variant is created with manage_inventory: true (SKU copied at that moment); matching is fully automatic via SKU with no human mapping step; and the SKU-RENAME HAZARD from bead MedusaOngoingWarehousePlugin-bkh (renaming a variant SKU leaves the inventory item on the old SKU and silently orphans inbound stock sync). title: Daily safety-check sweep: re-sync done orders (above threshold) changed in the past 24h
description:
Why: Companion to MedusaOngoingWarehousePlugin-8rg (stop re-syncing orders above the configurable 'done' threshold, default 450). Once done orders are excluded from the 15-minute status poll, any late change in Ongoing — a pickup order advancing 451 Klar til henting → 500 Hentet, a 475 Retur, corrected tracking, an annulment — would go unseen. A low-frequency safety net is needed.

What: Once every 24 hours (new cron job or a daily branch inside status-poll, gated per-integration like last_status_poll_at), query Ongoing for orders with status code above the SAME configurable threshold introduced in -8rg that have changes within the past 24 hours, and run the normal refresh/shipment/delivery sync path for each. This is a reconciliation pass: idempotent workflows (shipped_at / delivered_at guards) make redundant re-syncs no-ops. Check whether the Ongoing API supports a changed-since filter (e.g. lastChangedFrom on the orders endpoint) so the sweep doesn't fetch the entire done history; if not, bound the query window server-side as tightly as the API allows and filter client-side.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sweep runs once per 24h per integration (persisted last-run stamp + sync lock, matching existing job patterns).
- Uses the same configurable threshold variable as -8rg, not a second knob.
- Only orders changed in the past 24h are re-synced; the sweep is idempotent.
- A 451→500 pickup transition that the main poll now misses is picked up by the sweep (test).
- Rate-limit friendly: goes through the existing per-credential-key Throttle.
- docs/wiki updated (User-Sync-Reference.md job table).
notes:
Implemented (uncommitted, pending review). Design: the sweep is a DAILY SECOND PASS INSIDE status-poll.ts, not a new cron file — it reuses the poll's OngoingClient (same per-credential throttle), its status_poll lock, and one shared per-order apply function (applyTrackedOrder), so only one new column was needed.

API answer (the bead asked): GET /api/v1/orders DOES support a changed-since filter — 'orderStatusChangedTimeFrom' (only orders whose status changed after this time). Live-verified against the sandbox (2 new cases in client.live.test.ts): accepted, narrows the result set, and — unlike stockInfoChangedFrom — carries NO 24h age limit. Chose it over orderUpdatedTimeFrom (which is capped at 2 days old and semantically 'any update', not 'status changed').

Mechanics: gate = last_done_sweep_at (new OngoingIntegration column, Migration20260730220418) >= 24h; query = getOrdersByStatus(doneThreshold+1, 1000, now-26h) — same getDoneStatusThreshold() as 8rg, no second knob; 1000 included so a late annulment is caught. Lookback is 26h (> the 24h interval) because the sweep can only fire on a poll tick. Row scope = all NON-TERMINAL rows including done_synced_at-stamped ones, minus those the poll pass already applied this tick. Per-order failures are caught+logged and the sweep is STILL stamped (a poison row must not turn a daily pass into a per-tick one); a failed query leaves it unstamped so the next tick retries. Lock TTL raised to >=15min on a sweep tick.

title: Stop re-syncing orders above the configurable 'done' status threshold (default 450)
description:
Why: The status-poll job (src/jobs/status-poll.ts) sweeps Ongoing's full 100–999 band every 15 minutes and re-runs refreshOngoingOrderStatusWorkflow for every tracked order whose sync_state is not delivered/cancelled. Orders that Ongoing considers finished (status code above 450 — 451 Klar til henting, 475 Retur, 500 Hentet, 1000 Annullert) keep getting re-synced on every tick even though nothing more should happen to them. That wastes API calls against Ongoing's rate limits and churns the sync ledger.

What: Introduce a configurable 'done' status threshold (default 450) — as an OngoingIntegration column and/or plugin option, consistent with how shipped_status_codes/delivered_status_codes are configured today. Once an order has been observed at a status code above the threshold AND synced once at that status, mark its OngoingOrderSync row so subsequent poll ticks skip it (extend the TERMINAL_SYNC_STATES exclusion or add a done_at/last done-sync marker). It must still be synced exactly once at/after crossing the threshold so the final status/tracking lands in Medusa.
design: Interaction to resolve: bead 18m deliberately kept 'shipped' (450) non-terminal so pickup orders can advance 450/451 → 500 (Hentet). With 'above 450 = done', a 451 (Klar til henting) order would be frozen before its 500 delivered signal arrives — the companion 24h safety-check sweep (filed alongside this issue) is the intended catch-net for that transition; the two issues share the same threshold variable and should be designed together.
acceptance_criteria:
- A configurable threshold (default 450) exists; validated at boot like other options.
- An order above the threshold is synced exactly once after crossing it; subsequent status-poll ticks skip it.
- Orders at or below the threshold keep current behavior.
- Unit tests cover: crossing the threshold (one sync), already-done rows skipped, threshold configurability.
- docs/wiki updated (User-Sync-Reference.md, User-Configuration-Reference.md).
notes:
Implemented (uncommitted, pending review). Design: threshold is a PLUGIN OPTION only — defaultDoneStatusThreshold (default 450, boot-validated in options.ts, read via OngoingModuleService.getDoneStatusThreshold()). No per-integration column: the AC allows 'column and/or plugin option', and 'validated at boot' maps to the option; a per-integration knob would have meant migration + 2 validator files + 3 admin form files for a value that rarely differs per warehouse. t36 must use the same getter.

Skip marker: new OngoingOrderSync.done_synced_at (Migration20260730195522). status-poll excludes stamped rows alongside TERMINAL_SYNC_STATES. The stamp is written by a new markOrderSyncDoneWorkflow called LAST in the per-order block, so a failed refresh/shipment/delivery leaves the row unstamped and the next tick retries instead of freezing it half-synced. Comparison is strictly '>' so 450 keeps current behaviour (450 -> 500 pickup still polls). Webhook path deliberately ignores done_synced_at.

title: Interpret Ongoing status codes semantically (shipped vs delivered; pickup 450→500)
description:
The plugin currently decides an order is 'shipped' purely by membership in the per-integration shipped_status_codes list, with no understanding of Ongoing's canonical status lifecycle. This is fragile, easy to misconfigure, and does not model the pickup-order two-step.

Known semantics (see https://docs.ongoingwarehouse.com/manuals/statuses):
- 400 = order picked at warehouse
- 450 = order sent
- 500 = order picked up at pickup point
- Pickup orders progress 450 (sent) -> 500 (picked up).

Problem to solve:
- Map codes to a semantic STAGE (picked / shipped / delivered/picked-up) instead of a single flat 'shipped' membership test.
- 450 (sent) is the point to create the Medusa shipment + tracking. 500 (picked up) is a delivered/terminal signal for pickup orders and must be recorded WITHOUT being dropped: today markOrderSyncShippedStep sets shipped_at, and loadSyncForShipmentStep then short-circuits every later poll/webhook as already_shipped (terminal states shipped/cancelled stop refresh) — so the 450->500 transition on a pickup order is currently lost.
- Consider deriving sensible default shipped/delivered codes from Ongoing's canonical status list (GET /orders/statuses) rather than requiring each operator to hand-pick shipped_status_codes.
- Confirm 425 (Sendt/Dellevert) and 451 (Klar til henting / ready for pickup) placement in the same model.

Docs to update in the same change: docs/wiki/User-Sync-Reference.md (status-code interpretation section) and docs/wiki/User-Ongoing-Concepts.md (order statuses).
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented mapping of the canonical Ongoing status codes (400/425/450/451/500 at minimum) to plugin behavior (picked / shipped / delivered).
- A pickup order that goes 450 -> 500 creates the Medusa shipment at 450 AND records the 500 pickup (delivered) without error or a dropped transition.
- The shipped_at / terminal-state short-circuit no longer silently swallows a legitimate post-shipped 'picked up' signal.
- Unit/integration tests cover the 450->500 pickup path and the shipped-vs-delivered distinction.
- User-Sync-Reference and User-Ongoing-Concepts updated to match.

title: Ongoing cancel refusal no longer blocks the Medusa fulfillment cancel (ei4 trade-off)
description:
ei4 moved Ongoing cancellation out of the fulfillment provider (module-isolated, cannot run the status-gated workflow) into the app-scope order.fulfillment_canceled subscriber. The provider's cancelFulfillment is now a non-throwing no-op.

Consequence: when Ongoing's status is NOT in cancellable_status_codes, the plugin declines to cancel the Ongoing order, but Medusa has already set fulfillment.canceled_at. Previously the provider threw and kept canceled_at unset, so the two systems stayed consistent. Now they can disagree while Ongoing keeps shipping.

Needs a design decision on how to surface/reconcile: e.g. a dedicated sync_state or admin-dashboard alert for 'Ongoing refused the cancel', an ops runbook step, or a pre-cancel check in a fulfillment-module workflow hook that CAN veto.

title: P1-e: Translate DB unique-constraint violation to MedusaError in create/update Ongoing integration (I6/I7)
description:
Scoped OUT of #114's type-only passes by the #114 design doc (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-04-tighten-any-type-holes-at-module-boundaries-114-design.md), which explicitly says to file this as its own issue because it is a code-generation/DTO shape problem plus a behavior change, not a boundary-typing hole.

## Sites
- src/workflows/steps/create-ongoing-integration-row.ts (I6) — 'input as any'
- src/workflows/steps/update-ongoing-integration.ts (I7) — 'input as any' on update + compensation

## Two folded concerns
1. **DTO shape mismatch (type):** the generated create/update DTO types shipped_status_codes/cancellable_status_codes as Record<string,unknown>|null while the model.json() column is actually number[]|null, so the author cast 'input as any'. Decide: change the model column typing / add a typed input DTO, vs keep a narrow documented cast.
2. **Behavior — unique-constraint translation (I6):** a DB-level unique-constraint violation on create is NOT translated to a MedusaError type, so the admin API returns an opaque 500 instead of a 409/422. Catch the unique violation in the step and rethrow as MedusaError(MedusaError.Types.DUPLICATE_ERROR / NOT_ALLOWED) so the route surfaces a proper status.

## Acceptance
- create-ongoing-integration-row no longer uses 'input as any'; duplicate credential_key (or whatever the unique key is) returns a typed MedusaError -> non-500 HTTP status, with a regression test.
- update-ongoing-integration handler + compensation no longer use 'input as any'.
- node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit clean; tests pass.
close_reason: Merged PR #131. Removed input-wide 'as any' (field-level cast on the two model.json() columns) in create+update steps (I7). create step now re-tags a unique violation to MedusaError(DUPLICATE_ERROR)/422 (I6) — corrected premise: Medusa already maps 23505 to INVALID_DATA/400, so isUniqueViolation detects the mapped shape + raw edge. title: P3: Extract shared subscriber helper: persist-then-emit ordering and isolated event-bus try/catch
description:
Cross-shard epic from whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (P3). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## Pattern

Two problems folded into one root cause across all three subscribers:

1. **Emit failures mis-labeled.** `eventBus.emit(...)` is called inside the same try/catch as the state-persisting workflow. If emit throws after the workflow already succeeded, the catch logs it as "workflow failed" — mis-attributing an event-bus outage to the workflow.

2. **Edit-blocked branches emit BEFORE persisting state.** In `order-updated.ts` and `order-edit-confirmed.ts`, the blocked branch calls `eventBus.emit(EDIT_BLOCKED, ...)` **before** `markOrderSyncEditBlockedWorkflow(...).run(...)`. If the emit throws, the state-persisting workflow is skipped entirely — the row's `edit_blocked_at`/`category`/`reason` never get written even though the blocking decision was correct.

## Instances (I10)

- `src/subscribers/order-updated.ts:140-148,194-202`
- `src/subscribers/order-edit-confirmed.ts:78-87`
- `src/subscribers/order-canceled.ts:76-84`

## Precedent

`src/jobs/stock-sync.ts:100-119` and `src/jobs/retry-failed-syncs.ts:90-105,140-153` already do this right: they wrap `eventBus.emit(...)` in its own try/catch with an explicit comment noting an event-bus outage must not surface as a "row/integration failed" log for work that actually succeeded. Persist first, emit in its own isolated try.

## Recommended fix

Extract a shared `processSyncRows(rows, handler, logger, eventLabel)` helper (or an `emitDomainEvent(bus, event, payload)` helper) that:
- Runs the state-persisting workflow first.
- Only after success, emits the domain event in its own try/catch with a distinct log line ("failed to emit X — workflow succeeded").
- Collapses the duplicated per-row try/catch + logging boilerplate across all three subscribers.

Also collapses the related Minor finding on duplicated boilerplate across the three subscribers.

## Individual sub-issues

One sub-task per subscriber file to migrate to the shared helper.

title: P2: Uniform admin-UI loading/error/empty states via shared query hook
description:
Cross-shard epic from whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (P2). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## Pattern

Operator-facing admin surfaces uniformly treat "fetch failed" as "empty state". On the failed-syncs dashboard specifically this is the worst-case UX — a page whose entire job is surfacing failures fails silently.

## Instances

- `src/admin/routes/ongoing/page.tsx:200-239` — ConnectionHealthPanel query destructures only `data`/`isLoading`, never `isError`. Failed fetch renders "No Ongoing integrations configured yet." (I14).
- `src/admin/routes/ongoing/page.tsx:253-260` — OngoingSyncsTable query, same pattern. Failed fetch renders empty DataTable identical to "0 failed syncs" (I14).
- `src/admin/routes/settings/ongoing/page.tsx:28` — Integrations query, same pattern (I11).
- `src/admin/routes/settings/ongoing/create-integration-modal.tsx:38` — `credentialKeys`/`stockLocations` queries fetched with `enabled: open` but `isLoading`/`isFetching` never surfaced. Selects render empty option lists indistinguishable from "server has no credential keys" (I13).

Contrast: `src/admin/widgets/ongoing-order-sync.tsx:100-130` **does** correctly destructure and render `isError` — so the pattern already exists in the codebase, applied inconsistently.

## Recommended fix

Extract one shared `useOngoingQuery` wrapper (or a small render-helper) that always exposes `{ data, isLoading, isError, isEmpty }` with prescribed UI for each state. Migrate the three pages + one modal to use it. Prevents future recurrence at any new admin surface.

## Individual sub-issues

Break into per-surface sub-tasks once the shared hook shape is agreed. Track under this issue via native sub-issue relationship.

title: P1: Tighten "any" type holes at every module boundary (Ongoing REST / query.graph / container.resolve)
description:
Cross-shard epic from whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (P1). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## Pattern

The `any` type-hole shortcut was adopted consistently across every module boundary. Its cost surfaces as three independent type holes today and a compile-clean landmine for every future refactor.

## Instances

- `src/lib/ongoing/client.ts:155` — `mapInventoryRow(raw: any)` (I1)
- `src/lib/ongoing/client.ts:170` — `mapTrackedOrder(raw: any)` (I2)
- `src/lib/ongoing/re-query-fulfillment-order.ts:34` — `query: any` (I3)
- `src/workflows/steps/create-ongoing-integration-row.ts:40` — `input as any` (I6, hides unique-constraint MedusaError)
- `src/workflows/steps/update-ongoing-integration.ts:56, 79` — `input as any` on update + compensation (I7)
- Plus **45+ instances** of `container: any` / `service: any` across `src/workflows/steps/*.ts` (Shard-3 finding S3-M-any).
- Plus `eventBus as any` in the 3 subscribers and 2 jobs (Shard-5 finding).

## Failure modes

- Fields that Ongoing omits at runtime (e.g. `article` on inventory rows) flow into required fields silently — downstream code that keys off them operates on `undefined` and drops/mis-attributes state (I1, I2).
- Renaming a method or field on the module service is compile-clean everywhere the resolved value is `any` — bugs only surface at runtime as "not a function" or silent dropped writes.
- DB-level unique-constraint violations aren't translated to MedusaError types → API returns opaque 500 instead of 409 (I6).

## Recommended approach

- Introduce runtime validation at the Ongoing edge (Zod / valibot / io-ts) so `raw: any` becomes a typed schema at the boundary of `client.ts`.
- Generate types for `container.resolve(ONGOING_MODULE)` from the module service signatures, or type the resolve call site explicitly (`resolve<OngoingModuleService>(ONGOING_MODULE)`).
- Type the resolve of `Modules.EVENT_BUS` with a narrow local interface (as done selectively elsewhere in the codebase).
- Do this as one epic so the boundary types are consistent across the codebase, not in per-file drips.

## Individual sub-issues

Break this epic into sub-tasks per boundary once the approach is decided (client → module → step → subscriber). Track under this issue via the native sub-issue relationship.

Prior sub-issues (P1-a Zod REST edge, P1-b container:any 22 sites, P1-c EVENT_BUS, P1-d query:any, .1 unique-constraint MedusaError) closed earlier; this session cleaned up the remaining ~14 sibling holes in src/workflows/steps/*.ts (logger:any→Logger, container.resolve(...) as any→OngoingModuleService, Modules.INVENTORY→narrow InventoryServiceLike, 5x context as any→plain context) and re-query-fulfillment-order.ts (i:any→RawFulfillmentItem). title: Audit createOrderShipmentWorkflow side effects for duplicate-on-outer-retry paths (residual from CRIT-5)
description:
Residual from review CRIT-5 refutation (2026-07-02). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## File
`src/workflows/steps/apply-order-shipment.ts` (invocation) — audit target is `node_modules/@medusajs/core-flows/dist/order/workflows/create-order-shipment.js` behavior

## Context

The review flagged apply-order-shipment.ts:51 for nesting `createOrderShipmentWorkflow(container).run(...)` inside a step handler (CRIT-5 original claim). Adversarial refute showed this is a documented Medusa pattern (Medusa's own core-flows do the same, e.g. `cancelOrderWorkflow` invoked from `complete-cart.js:141`) — `.run()` executes the inner workflow's own saga (including its step compensations). So the "nested workflow breaks compensation" framing is refuted.

**But the refuter surfaced a narrower residual:** if `createOrderShipmentWorkflow` succeeds (shipment created + `SHIPMENT_CREATED` event emitted + potential customer notification since `no_notification: false`) but the outer `syncOngoingShipmentWorkflow` later step (`markOrderSyncShippedStep`) fails, a retry re-runs the outer workflow. The "already shipped" MedusaError catch prevents re-creating the shipment, but any side effects **not gated by that check** could re-fire on retry.

## Task

Audit `createOrderShipmentWorkflow`'s side effects and identify any that:
1. Fire outside the shipment-creation transaction that the "already shipped" catch guards.
2. Could produce duplicate customer-visible outcomes on retry (duplicate notification email, duplicate webhook, duplicate analytics event).

If any such path exists, add an idempotency guard (dedupe key, has-notified-flag on the sync row, etc.) so outer-workflow retries don't re-fire the side effect.

If no such path exists, close this issue with a note explaining what was audited and why it's safe.

title: Add compare-and-swap on retry_count in retry-failed-syncs.ts to avoid double-increment under multi-instance overlap (residual from CRIT-7)
description:
Residual from review CRIT-7 refutation (2026-07-02). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## File
`src/jobs/retry-failed-syncs.ts:156-193`

## Context

The whole-project review flagged retry-failed-syncs.ts for missing `acquireSyncLock`/`releaseSyncLock` versus its sibling jobs `status-poll.ts` and `stock-sync.ts` (CRIT-7 original claim). Adversarial refute confirmed the "duplicate Ongoing order push" consequence doesn't hold — `pushOrderRecordSyncStep` calls `client.putOrder(model)` which is explicitly an idempotent upsert keyed by `ongoing_order_number`. The plan doc for #39 self-documents this choice.

**But the refuter surfaced a narrower residual:** two overlapping ticks (multi-instance deployment, or a slow tick still running past the next minute boundary) can both pass the `isRetryDue` check and both increment `retry_count`. There's no compare-and-swap. Result: double-increment of the retry counter and double Ongoing API calls for that row.

## Failure scenario

Two `retry-failed-syncs` job instances run on overlapping ticks. Both list the same due row (`sync_state: 'error'`, `error_class: 'retryable'`, `next_retry_at < now`). Both invoke `pushOrderToOngoing`. The Ongoing PUT is idempotent so no duplicate order is created — but `retry_count` is incremented twice via `service.updateOrderSync({retry_count: current + 1})` in a plain last-write-wins pattern. Backoff computations for the next retry are now wrong (potentially skips a due window or halves the interval).

Not data corruption. But it distorts backoff and doubles Ongoing rate-limit consumption for that row.

## Recommended fix

- Add a compare-and-swap on `retry_count` (`WHERE retry_count = expected AND sync_state = 'error'`), or
- Add a per-row lock scoped to the due-window processing (analogous to `acquireSyncLock` but keyed per-row instead of per-integration).

The plan for #39 explicitly opted out of the sibling-job lock; this narrower fix targets the actual leftover race.

title: Narrow terminal-error swallow in cancelOngoingOrderStep to specific 'already cancelled' shape (residual from CRIT-3)
description:
Residual from review CRIT-3 refutation (2026-07-02). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## File
`src/workflows/steps/cancel-ongoing-order.ts:29-36`

## Context

The whole-project review flagged the client-level DELETE retry as mis-classifying "already cancelled" as terminal (CRIT-3 original claim). Adversarial refute found that the step already catches `err instanceof OngoingApiError && err.kind === 'terminal'` and returns `StepResponse({cancelled:false, swallowed:true})` — idempotent-success handler. So the specific claim is refuted.

**But the refuter surfaced a narrower residual:** the swallow keys on `kind === 'terminal'` (any 4xx), not on the specific "already cancelled" message match. A genuinely-different 400 error (malformed order id, permissions issue, contract violation) is silently swallowed as a false success too.

## Failure scenario

Ongoing returns 400 with a `not-yet-implemented feature` / `unauthorized order id format` error (not "already cancelled"). The step catches it as `kind: 'terminal'` and returns `{cancelled: false, swallowed: true}` as a success. The workflow proceeds to `markOrderSyncCancelledStep` and writes an incorrect terminal state — the merchant's cancel appears successful, but no cancellation actually happened at Ongoing.

## Recommended fix

Narrow the swallow to match the specific Ongoing error shape/message for "already cancelled" only. All other terminal 4xx should re-throw or classify as a real failure so the retry-failed-syncs workflow can surface them.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #130 (squash-merged to main). Narrowed cancelOngoingOrderStep swallow to already-cancelled message shape; all other terminal 4xx re-throw. Medusa-aware review done; review fix (log Ongoing's own reason) applied.

title: Retry driver must cap on OngoingOrderSync.retry_count (dead-letter deterministic failures)
description:
Forward note from the #67/#73 review. #67 made unknown/network errors classify as `retryable` (correct — avoids dead-lettering on transient outages). Consequence: once a **retry driver** is built (re-runs sync rows with `error_class = "retryable"`), a *deterministic* non-network failure (a programming bug, or malformed-but-non-`OngoingApiError` data) would be retried forever instead of dead-lettering.

The `OngoingOrderSync` model already has a `retry_count` column (default 0), so the design anticipates a cap. **Requirement for the retry driver:** honor `retry_count` as a max-attempts ceiling — after N attempts, stop retrying and mark the row terminal/dead-lettered.

No consumer exists yet (no retry driver in M2). Tracking so it isn't lost when the retry mechanism lands. Related: #67.

title: Classify unknown/network errors as retryable in Ongoing sync (not terminal)
description:
Surfaced in the #26 Medusa review. In `pushOrderRecordSyncHandler` (and the client retry loop), errors are classified via `err instanceof OngoingApiError ? err.kind : undefined`, so a raw network error (ECONNRESET / timeout / DNS / a `fetch` TypeError) yields `undefined` → `error_class = "terminal"`. The client `request()` retry loop also only retries `OngoingApiError` with `kind: "retryable"`. Net effect: a brief outage permanently flags the sync row `terminal` and requires manual intervention.

This matched the plan's explicit decision and was non-blocking for #26 because the retry consumer (#21) isn't built yet. Fix before #21 relies on it: classify unknown/non-API/network errors as `retryable` (or detect transient network failures explicitly) so they get retried rather than dead-lettered.

Follow-up to #26; consumer is #21.

title: Fix lint failures in ongoing module service.ts (sync accessors + generic Error)
description:
`yarn lint` is red on `main` due to code merged in #52 (`src/modules/ongoing/service.ts`):

- 2 errors — `@medusajs/service-methods-must-be-async` on `getCredentials` and `getClient` (lines 20, 28)
- 1 warning — `@medusajs/use-medusa-error-not-generic-error` on the `throw new Error(...)` (line 23)

CI does not currently run lint (only `superpowers-guards.yml`), so this didn't block merges, but it surfaces in every agent's verification and leaves `main` failing `yarn lint`.

**Fix approach:** `getCredentials`/`getClient` are pure synchronous accessors (in-memory config lookup + client construction, no I/O); the async rule targets DB-backed service methods. Keep them synchronous (forcing `async` would ripple `await` to all call sites, including in-flight work) and suppress the rule with a justifying comment. Swap the generic `Error` for `MedusaError(INVALID_DATA, ...)`.

Surfaced during M2 Wave 2 (#23). Follow-up to #52.

title: Validate the edit-sync-rules JSON and the interval fields in the form, not only on submit
description:
Follow-up from the field-help-text epic (4ng), deliberately left out of it because that epic was copy-only.

Two inputs accept text that is only judged later, or never:

- Edit sync rules (JSON): parseEditSyncRulesJson runs on Save. A typo means filling in the rest of the form, pressing Save, and reading an error at the bottom. Validate on blur and show the parse error next to the field. The shape is known (an object of category -> number[]), so a shape check beyond JSON.parse is cheap and catches the more common mistake: valid JSON, wrong schema.
- Stock sync / status poll interval: the create and update routes only check that the value is a string. A non-numeric value is accepted, stored, and then silently ignored at read time (resolveIntervalMs falls back to the default), so the operator sees a saved value that does nothing. Keep the help text and any new error copy in sync (Documentation-Guidelines).

title: Stamp each build so "is the app running my build?" is answerable
description:
The package version is 0.0.1 and never moves between local builds, so there is no way to ask a linked app which build it is running. Today the only reliable check is grepping node_modules for a string you happen to have just written — which only works if you wrote a distinctive one, and not at all for a colleague reproducing a report.

Wanted: the build writes a marker the app can be asked for — a build id (timestamp + short git sha, dirty flag) emitted into the built output and readable at runtime. Options to weigh: a generated constant in the built server output, an extra field on the packaged package.json, and/or logging it at module boot next to the existing "[ongoing] validated N warehouse integration(s)" line so the app tells you in the boot log.

A boot-log line is probably the highest value: it makes the answer visible without shell archaeology in node_modules, and it is what an operator can paste into a bug report. Keep it out of the published-to-registry path if it would make builds non-reproducible.

Consumed by the verify step of the parent bead.
acceptance_criteria: A local build is identifiable from the consuming app without inspecting node_modules by hand; the update script can assert that a given app is running a specific build.

title: Per-order retry for a failed done-order sweep reconciliation
description:
Why: the daily done-order sweep (t36, src/jobs/status-poll.ts) isolates per-order failures — it logs them, counts them, and stamps last_done_sweep_at anyway so one poison row can't turn the daily pass into a per-tick one. The consequence, made explicit in the code comment and the log line, is that the failed order's reconciliation is DROPPED: the next sweep's window starts at the new stamp, so unless that order's status changes again in Ongoing, the missed transition is never re-applied. Raised in the PR#158 review (finding B3).

What: give the sweep a bounded per-order retry rather than a single best-effort attempt. Options to weigh: (a) record the failure on the OngoingOrderSync row (a sweep_failed_at / sweep_retry_count pair) and have the next sweep union those rows into its candidate set regardless of the changed-since window; (b) reuse the existing error/retryable ledger + retry-failed-syncs backoff machinery, which today only covers pushes, not reconciliation reads; (c) hold last_done_sweep_at back to the oldest failed order's change time, accepting a wider next window. (a) is probably the smallest honest fix.

Not urgent: it only bites when an above-threshold order both changes late AND fails to apply, and the failure is loud in the logs.
acceptance_criteria: A per-order sweep failure is retried on a later sweep without depending on the order changing again in Ongoing; the retry is bounded (no unbounded re-attempt loop); the drop-warning log line and the code comment in sweepDoneOrders are updated to match the new behaviour; unit-tested.

title: Retry classification: 408 terminal and Retry-After HTTP-date form unhandled
description:
Two small gaps in the Ongoing client retry handling:
- errors.ts:9-14 classifyHttpStatus only treats 429 and >=500 as retryable, so a 408 Request Timeout (some gateways/WAFs emit it on slow client writes) falls through to terminal and is not retried. Client-side network timeouts are already covered by AbortController/classifyError, so this only matters if Ongoing's stack emits 408 explicitly.
- client.ts:430-436 parseRetryAfter only handles the delta-seconds form. Per RFC 7231 Retry-After may also be an HTTP-date; Number(dateString) yields NaN -> undefined, silently falling back to exponential backoff instead of honoring the server delay.
acceptance_criteria: 408 is classified retryable (or a documented decision not to); parseRetryAfter also handles the HTTP-date form (or a code comment records the seconds-only assumption); tests cover both.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in #151

title: Ongoing client retry backoff has no jitter
description: Both retry layers use purely deterministic exponential backoff: transport-layer client.ts:82 (250 * 2**attempt) and ledger-layer computeRetryBackoffMs (retry-policy.ts:118-125). Under a shared Ongoing outage (5xx blip across many goods owners/orders), retrying clients and cron ticks back off in lockstep, producing synchronized retry bursts. Per-credential-key Throttle (concurrency 1) mitigates within a key, but the ledger-layer backoff spans many independent workflow invocations across orders.
acceptance_criteria: A randomized jitter factor is applied to backoff (at least the ledger-layer computeRetryBackoffMs); existing backoff tests updated to tolerate/inject the jitter.

title: Return push has no retry backstop (no OngoingOrderSync ledger row for returns)
description:
Unlike the outbound order push, pushReturnOrderToOngoing writes NO OngoingOrderSync row — it only emits RETURN_ORDER_PUSH_FAILED. So a failed return push is logged and dropped: retry-failed-syncs has nothing to sweep.

This mattered less when the push ran synchronously inside the provider's createReturnFulfillment (the throw aborted the return fulfillment). ei4 moved it into the app-scope order.return_requested subscriber, which never throws — so a transient Ongoing outage now silently loses the return push with no automatic recovery.

Give returns a ledger row (or an equivalent retryable record) so the retry job covers them.
acceptance_criteria: A failed return push leaves a retryable record that retry-failed-syncs picks up, with the same backoff/dead-letter semantics as the order push.
notes: Returns now reuse OngoingOrderSync via a sync_kind discriminator ('order' default | 'return') instead of a separate model — gives returns the SAME retry-failed-syncs backoff/dead-letter machinery for free. Changes: model + Migration20260725130000 (text check enum, default 'order') + snapshot; RecordSyncInput gains sync_kind; push-return-order.ts records pending->error/sent (mirrors push-order-record-sync, keyed by returnOrderNumber, return fulfillment id in medusa_fulfillment_id); retry-failed-syncs job branches re-push on sync_kind (return -> pushReturnOrderToOngoing({return_fulfillment_id})). Guard: order-detail /sync route filters sync_kind='order' so the widget's order-Re-push can't wrongly fire on a return row; return rows stay visible + retryable via the syncs dashboard (bulk-retry goes through the sync_kind-aware job). Tests: return-branch retry test, push-return workflow ledger assertions (pending/sent, error/retryable), route filter assertion. Full L1 641 pass; L2 validated (ongoing-module boot applies migrations; push-order recordSync round-trips 'sent'/'error' against real PG). Docs: Dev-Architecture return-sync ledger section rewritten (outbound resolved, inbound still events-only). Unblocked now that 2a6 confirmed the PUT /returnOrders response id.
close_reason: A failed return push now lands an error/retryable OngoingOrderSync row (sync_kind='return') that retry-failed-syncs re-pushes via the return workflow with identical backoff/dead-letter semantics. Acceptance met; L2-validated.

title: Exchange/claim return legs are not pushed to Ongoing (order.exchange_created / order.claim_created not wired)
description:
The ei4 return push subscriber (src/subscribers/return-created.ts) listens on order.return_requested only. Core emits that from confirm-return-request and create-complete-return, but the return legs of an EXCHANGE and a CLAIM emit order.exchange_created / order.claim_created instead. Those returns therefore never reach Ongoing.

Wire the same push (resolve the return fulfillment via the return_fulfillment link -> return.fulfillments, gate on provider_id prefix 'ongoing_', run pushReturnOrderToOngoing) for those events, or find a shared downstream event that covers all three.
acceptance_criteria: An exchange return and a claim return each produce a PUT /returnOrders call to Ongoing, covered by subscriber unit tests.
notes: Extracted the resolve/gate/push return body into src/lib/push-return-to-ongoing.ts (pushReturnToOngoing + resolveReturnIdFor). return-created.ts now delegates; added exchange-created.ts (order.exchange_created) and claim-created.ts (order.claim_created) subscribers that resolve the entity's return_id (query.graph on order_exchange/order_claim, return_id FK with return.id fallback) then run the shared push. Outbound-only exchange / refund-only claim => no return id => no-op. Unit tests: exchange-created.test.ts + claim-created.test.ts (11 cases) assert pushReturnOrderToOngoing.run is called with the resolved return_fulfillment_id, provider gating, no-op paths, never-throws. Helper moved to src/lib because the @medusajs eslint subscriber-default-export rule applies to direct children of src/subscribers only. Full L1 640 pass, lint+build clean.

title: Clear edit-blocked state on successful re-sync (banner goes stale otherwise)
description:
## Context

Surfaced by the M5 cross-plan review of #93 (widget banner) + #94 (order-updated post-workflow persist).

**Consequence:** once a row is marked edit-blocked, a subsequent successful re-sync never nulls `edit_blocked_at` / `edit_blocked_category` / `edit_blocked_reason`. So the order-widget "Edit blocked" banner (#93) becomes **permanently sticky** in production — it will keep showing even after the edit successfully re-syncs.

## Proposed fix

On the success path of each edit re-sync (the `if (result?.synced)` branches in `src/subscribers/order-updated.ts` and `src/subscribers/order-edit-confirmed.ts`), call `markOrderSyncEditBlockedWorkflow(container).run({ input: { order_sync_id: row.id, blocked: false } })` to null the three fields (the workflow/step already support `blocked: false` per #91).

- #91 (persisted the fields + wired the workflow; clear-on-success was its optional Task 6)
- #93 (renders the banner that would go stale)
- #94 (adds the order-updated post-workflow persist site)

title: pre-push hook blocks all non-fast-forward pushes, forcing branch delete+recreate on rebase
description:
## Problem

`scripts/pre-push` rejects **any** non-fast-forward push, with no exception for rebasing your own feature branch. When an open PR's branch is rebased onto an advanced `main` (a normal way to resolve merge conflicts), `git push --force-with-lease` is rejected by the hook.

## Impact

During M5 wave-1, PR #96 (issue #44) needed a rebase after sibling PR #95 (#91) merged and touched the same subscriber files. The force-push was blocked, so the branch had to be **deleted and recreated** (which the hook permits — it skips the ancestor check when the remote ref is freshly created). GitHub then auto-closes a PR whose head branch is deleted and refuses to reopen one whose branch was recreated, so a **new PR (#99)** had to be opened to replace #96. This adds churn (lost PR history/discussion, new number) every time a PR needs a post-review rebase.

## Suggested fix

Scope the non-fast-forward block to **protected branches only** (e.g. `main`), and allow force-with-lease on feature branches. Alternatively, document the delete+recreate (and resulting new-PR) workaround in the process docs so it's a known, deliberate step rather than a surprise.

## Discovered by

M5 parallel wave execution (`/work-milestone`); surfaced when rebasing #96 → became #99. See also the `npx tsc` fake-success and RTK `git diff` compaction findings from the same run (separate concerns).

title: order-updated.ts: persist edit-blocked state when workflow's internal re-gate blocks (post-workflow site)
description:
## Context

Surfaced during code review of #91 (persist edit-blocked state on `OngoingOrderSync`).

`src/subscribers/order-edit-confirmed.ts` has **two** blocked-emit sites and #91 wires `markOrderSyncEditBlockedWorkflow` at both: the pre-check (`!allowed`) and the post-workflow site where `syncOrderEditToOngoing` itself returns `result.blocked === true` (a race where status changes between the subscriber's own query and the workflow's internal re-gate).

`src/subscribers/order-updated.ts` only ever had **one** blocked-emit site (the pre-check) before #91 — it never emitted `ongoing.sync.edit_blocked` at a post-workflow site, so #91 (which only wires *existing* emit sites) did not add persistence there either. Its post-workflow branch today is:

```ts
if (result?.synced) {
  logger.info(...)
} else {
  logger.warn(`... re-sync not applied ... (workflow: ${result?.reason ?? "unknown"})`)
  // no event emitted, no field write
}
```

`syncOrderEditToOngoing`'s result shape (`src/workflows/sync-order-edit-to-ongoing.ts:6-27`) already carries `{ synced, blocked, reason }`, so the data needed to detect and persist this case is available — it's just unused today.

## Proposed fix

Mirror `order-edit-confirmed.ts`'s post-workflow branch in `order-updated.ts`:
- When `result?.blocked` is true (or `!result?.synced`), emit `ongoing.sync.edit_blocked` (currently not emitted at all at this site — a separate, smaller gap) and call `markOrderSyncEditBlockedWorkflow(container).run({ input: { order_sync_id: row.id, blocked: true, category: "address_contact", reason: result?.reason ?? "status_blocked" } })`.

## Not in scope

Do not fold this into #91 — that PR intentionally scoped itself to wiring only the pre-existing emit sites literally in the issue text, to minimize merge-conflict surface with concurrent #42/#44 subscriber-file work.

title: Validate defaultStatusPollInterval (NaN guard) in status-poll job
description:
Surfaced by the independent Medusa review of PR #85 (issue #34).

`OngoingModuleService.getDefaultStatusPollIntervalMs()` does `parseInt(this.options_.defaultStatusPollInterval ?? "60000", 10)` with **no finite/>0 guard**, and `resolveIntervalMs` in `src/jobs/status-poll.ts` only validates the *per-integration* `status_poll_interval`, falling through to the default unchecked.

**Failure:** a misconfigured non-numeric `defaultStatusPollInterval` plugin option yields `NaN` → `isDue` (`now - last >= NaN`) is always false, so an integration polls **once then never again**, and `acquireSyncLock` stamps `new Date(now + NaN)` = `Invalid Date`. Silent (no error), config-time only.

**Fix:** apply the same `Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0` guard to the default branch (fall back to 60000), and/or validate `defaultStatusPollInterval` in `src/modules/ongoing/options.ts`.

Source: PR #85 / #34.
close_reason: Boot validation of defaultStatusPollInterval + parseIntervalMs NaN/<=0 fallback in getDefaultStatusPollIntervalMs and getDefaultStockSyncIntervalMs (defense-in-depth). Tests in interval-options.test.ts.

title: Webhook route: wrap post-auth handler body in try/catch to avoid 500 on transient errors
description:
Surfaced by the independent Medusa review of PR #80 (issue #35).

In `src/api/ongoing/webhooks/[credentialKey]/route.ts`, the **post-authentication** path (`req.scope.resolve(ONGOING_MODULE)`, `await listOngoingIntegrations(...)`, and the `shipped_status_codes as number[]` access on a `model.json().nullable()` column) is not wrapped — a DB/config error throws and surfaces as a **500**.

This is **only reachable after a valid X-Auth-Token**, so it is *not* an unauthenticated enumeration vector (the uniform-401 surface is intact). At worst a verified Ongoing delivery gets a 500 and is retried by Ongoing's retry policy.

**Recommendation:** wrap the post-auth body in try/catch and return a retry-friendly acknowledgement (consistent with the always-200, downstream-idempotent contract), logging the error server-side.

Likely best addressed alongside #36 (which fills the dispatch seam in this same handler's in-band branch). Source: PR #80 / #35; relates to #36.
close_reason: Wrapped webhook post-auth body (listOngoingIntegrations + nullable shipped_status_codes read + dispatch) in try/catch; transient error now logs + acks 200 per always-200 poll-backstopped contract. Test added.

title: Harden syncOngoingShipment idempotency against Medusa error-string coupling
description:
Surfaced by the independent Medusa review of PR #82 (issue #33).

`applyOrderShipmentStep` treats an already-shipped fulfillment as idempotent success by matching the **exact message string** `MedusaError(NOT_ALLOWED, "Shipment has already been created")` thrown by Medusa core-flow's `validate-shipment` step. Verified correct against pinned Medusa **2.16.0**.

**Risk:** a future Medusa version that rewords that message would silently flip the already-shipped case from *idempotent no-op* into a *recorded terminal error* on `OngoingOrderSync` — a regression with no compile-time or test signal (unit tests mock the core-flow).

**Options (low priority, defensive):**
- Add a comment pinning the assumption to the Medusa version, and/or
- Match on `err.type === MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED` plus a narrower signal instead of the full message, and/or
- Add an integration test against the real `createOrderShipmentWorkflow` that re-asserts the swallow contract, to fail loudly on a Medusa bump.

Source: PR #82 / #33. Not a current defect (2.16.0 is pinned).
close_reason: Decoupled already-shipped idempotency from exact error string; added regression test. Merged to main 373879d.

title: gate-order-edit collapses to first row when medusa_fulfillment_id is null (multi-row mis-targeting)
description:
Flagged independently by the Medusa reviews of #31 (PR #71) and #54 (PR #70).

**Root cause:** `src/workflows/steps/gate-order-edit.ts` — when `medusa_fulfillment_id` is null/absent, the gate falls back to `list({ medusa_order_id })[0]` (first row only). For an order with ≥2 `OngoingOrderSync` rows that all have null `medusa_fulfillment_id`, every per-row iteration in the order-edit / order.updated subscribers re-resolves to the *same first row*, so rows 2..N are mis-targeted.

**Reachability:** Low in M2 — `latest_status_code` defaults to null so the gate stays closed until status polling lands, and in practice each sync row carries a `medusa_fulfillment_id` from its pushed fulfillment. Becomes reachable once status polling populates `latest_status_code` AND a null-fulfillment multi-row order occurs.

**Fix:** target the gate by the sync row's own id (`order_sync_id` — the subscribers already have `row.id`) instead of collapsing to the first row by `medusa_order_id`.

Pre-existing contract gap in #27's gate step (not introduced by #31/#54). Consumers: #31, #54. Placed in M3 since it's only reachable once status polling exists.

title: Evaluate per-warehouse inventory (GET /articles/inventoryPerWarehouse) and multi-warehouse stock locations
description:
Deferred from epic MedusaOngoingWarehousePlugin-hhw. Recorded now so the endpoint tradeoff is not re-researched from scratch later.

The plugin's model is one goods owner (credential key) -> one Medusa stock location (stock_location_id is unique() on OngoingIntegration), and GET /articles returns inventory AGGREGATED ACROSS ALL WAREHOUSES for that goods owner. That is correct as long as the merchant treats 'Ongoing' as a single virtual location. It becomes wrong the moment a goods owner has more than one Ongoing warehouse and the merchant wants per-warehouse Medusa stock locations — the aggregate would over-report stock at each.

Ongoing offers GET /api/v1/articles/inventoryPerWarehouse for this: params goodsOwnerId, warehouseIds, articleSystemIdFrom, maxArticlesToGet, articleNumbers, onlyArticlesInStock, excludeStructureArticles, excludeNonStockArticles, stockInfoChangedFrom (same 24h cap). GetArticleInventoryPerWarehouseInfo carries warehouseId, numberOfItems, numberOfLockedItems, sellableNumberOfItems, availableForSaleNumberOfItems, reported, allocatedNumberOfItems.

The blocking tradeoff: that model has NO toReceiveNumberOfItems, which the current sync maps to Medusa incoming_quantity. Adopting it wholesale loses incoming-stock sync unless a second GET /articles call re-adds it — which doubles the request volume against an API that explicitly rate-limits concurrency (developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/parallel-requests). Its excludeStructureArticles / excludeNonStockArticles filters would, however, replace the client-side classification built in hhw.1 with a server-side one.

Do not start this without a real merchant needing multi-warehouse. Deciding it on the endpoint's merits alone would trade a working incoming_quantity sync for filters we already have.
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision is recorded on whether to support per-warehouse stock locations, with the incoming_quantity cost quantified.
- If yes: OngoingIntegration's one-location-per-credential-key constraint is revisited, since stock_location_id is currently unique().

title: Cleanup workflow for setup artifacts on integration delete
description: ⚠️ UNVERIFIED finding from 2026-07-17 docs research sweep — requires human review and verification before being worked on. delete-ongoing-integration.ts only deletes the OngoingIntegration row; the stock-location defineLink row, fulfillment set, service zone, and shipping option created by setupOngoingLocationWorkflow are left behind (admin delete prompt warns about this — known accepted gap). design:
Verified (2026-07-20): delete-ongoing-integration.ts deletes only the OngoingIntegration row via deleteOngoingIntegrationStep; setupOngoingLocationWorkflow creates a fulfillment set (only when reuse===false), a service zone, a shipping option, the integration-location column, and the OngoingIntegration<->stock_location remote link — all orphaned on delete.
